The lighter the start, the longer it tends to last, so you don't need to prepare perfectly from the beginning.

rows.ko: {{근거}} 때라, 다가오는 해는 새로운 시작에 활짝 열리는 해(순풍)입니다. 오래 망설이던 일도 막상 첫발을 떼면 생각보다 순조롭게 굴러가기 쉬워요. 새로 해 보고 싶은 일을 이미 하고 있는 사람의 이야기를 찾아 듣거나 직접 물어보세요. 다만 시작이 즐거운 만큼, 기존에 하던 일을 정리할 시간도 함께 마련해 두는 편이 좋습니다.
rows.en: Thanks to {{근거}}, the coming year is an Open Year for new beginnings. Plans you've hesitated over for ages roll along smoothly once you take that first step. Seek out stories from people already doing what you want to try, or reach out and ask them directly. Starting is a joy, so set aside time to wrap up what you already have going, too.
rows.en_before_tone: With {{근거}}, the coming year is a Wide-Open Year (Tailwind) for new starts. Even things you've hesitated over for a long time are likely to roll along more smoothly than expected once you take the first step. Try looking for stories from people already doing what you want to try, or asking them directly. Still, as much as starting is fun, it's good to also make time to wrap up what you've been doing.

rows.ko: 새 출발을 꿈꿔 왔다면 다가오는 해가 문을 활짝 열어 줄 수 있어요. 이 해는 새로운 시작이 활짝 열리는 해(순풍)입니다. {{근거}} 덕분에 처음 해 보는 일에도 도와줄 사람과 기회가 닿기 쉬워요. 낯선 동네를 걸어 보거나 처음 가 보는 모임에 참여하는 것처럼 익숙한 반경을 한 걸음 넓혀 보세요.
rows.en: If you've dreamed of a fresh start, the coming year throws the door wide open. It's an Open Year for new beginnings. With {{근거}}, supportive people step into your path and opportunities find you, even when everything is new. Widen your usual orbit by one step: wander an unfamiliar neighborhood or drop in on a group you've never joined.
rows.en_before_tone: If you've dreamed of a fresh start, the coming year may open the door wide for you. This year is a Wide-Open Year (Tailwind) for a new start. Thanks to {{근거}}, even for things you're trying for the first time, helpful people and opportunities are likely to come your way. Try stepping a little outside your usual circle, like walking an unfamiliar neighborhood or joining a gathering you've never been to.

rows.ko: 처음부터 다시 해 보고 싶은 일이 있다면, 다가오는 해는 새로운 시작이 활짝 열리는 해(순풍)입니다. {{근거}} 시기라 설렘이 두려움보다 조금 더 커지고, 첫걸음을 응원해 주는 흐름이 이어지기 쉬워요. 쓰지 않던 노트 한 권을 꺼내 첫 장에 이루고 싶은 모습을 적는 것으로 시작을 알려 보세요. 여러 갈래가 동시에 열릴 수 있으니 가장 마음이 가는 한 길을 먼저 골라 걷는 편이 좋습니다.
rows.en: If there's something you've longed to start from scratch, the coming year is an Open Year for a new start. Because of {{근거}}, the butterflies outweigh the fear, and the current keeps cheering you on after your first step. Mark the moment: open a fresh notebook and write the person you hope to become on the first page. Several paths open at once, so choose the one that pulls at your heart most and start there.
rows.en_before_tone: If there's something you want to start over from scratch, the coming year is a Wide-Open Year (Tailwind) for a new start. With {{근거}}, excitement is likely to grow a bit bigger than fear, and a flow that cheers on your first step tends to continue. You might mark the start by taking out an unused notebook and writing on the first page the person you hope to become. Several paths may open at once, so it can help to choose the one that draws your heart most and walk it first.

rows.ko: 다가오는 해는 새로운 시작이 내 손에 달린 해(보통)입니다. 돕는 힘과 무게가 엇비슷해, 언제 첫발을 떼느냐보다 떼고 나서 얼마나 이어 가느냐가 더 중요해지기 쉬워요. 시작하고 싶은 일을 하루 십 분짜리로 쪼개 이번 주에 세 번만 해 보세요.
rows.en: For a new start, the coming year is a Steady Year. The support and the weight balance out, so how long you keep going after the first step matters more than when you take it. Break what you want to begin into ten-minute pieces, and do it just three times this week.
rows.en_before_tone: The coming year is an In-Your-Hands Year (Steady) for a new start. Support and weight are about even, so how long you keep going after the first step tends to matter more than when you take it. Try breaking what you want to start into ten-minute pieces and doing it just three times this week.

rows.ko: 새로운 시작을 바란다면, 이 해는 출발의 때를 내가 고르는 내 손에 달린 해(보통)예요. 어느 한쪽 힘이 앞서지 않아, 준비가 되었다고 느끼는 순간을 스스로 정하는 힘이 필요합니다. ‘이것만 갖추면 시작한다’는 조건을 한 가지로 줄여 적어 보세요. 움직임이 많은 해라면 그 흐름이 첫걸음을 가볍게 밀어 줄 수도 있어요.
rows.en: If you're ready for a fresh start, this is a Steady Year, and you choose the moment you set out. Neither force pulls ahead, so you decide when you're ready. Cut your list of ‘I'll start once I have…’ conditions down to one, and write it down. If the year turns into a Moving Year, that motion gives your first step an extra nudge.
rows.en_before_tone: If you want a new start, this is an In-Your-Hands Year (Steady), when you choose the moment to set out. Neither force pulls ahead, so you need the strength to decide for yourself when you feel ready. Try narrowing your ‘I'll start once I have this’ conditions down to one and writing it down. If it's a Moving Year, that flow may give your first step a gentle push.

rows.ko: 새로운 시작은 다가오는 해에 기다림보다 작은 실행에서 열리기 쉬워요. 하늘의 흐름이 한쪽으로 쏠리지 않는 내 손에 달린 해(보통)라, 첫발의 크기보다 첫발을 뗐다는 사실이 중요합니다. 늘 다니던 길 대신 다른 길로 걸어 보거나 처음 먹어 보는 메뉴를 고르는 것처럼, 일상의 작은 처음부터 경험해 보세요.
rows.en: New beginnings in the coming year spring from small actions, not from waiting. It's a Steady Year, and the sky tilts neither way, so the simple fact that you took a first step outweighs how big it was. Collect small everyday firsts: take a different route, or order a dish you've never tried.
rows.en_before_tone: In the coming year, a new start is more likely to open through small action than through waiting. This is an In-Your-Hands Year (Steady), when the sky's flow doesn't lean to one side, so the fact that you took a first step matters more than its size. Try small firsts in daily life, like walking a different route than usual or ordering a dish you've never had.

rows.ko: 새로운 시작의 열쇠는 다가오는 해에 내 손에 쥐어져 있어요. 밀어주는 쪽과 붙잡는 쪽이 엇비슷한, 내 손에 달린 해(보통)이기 때문입니다. 함께 시작해 줄 사람 한 명을 찾아 서로의 첫걸음을 응원하는 약속을 해 보세요.
rows.en: The key to a fresh start sits in your own hands in the coming year. That's the nature of a Steady Year, where the push and the pull run even. Find one person to begin something with, and promise to cheer each other through those first steps.
rows.en_before_tone: In the coming year, the key to a new start is in your hands. That's because it's an In-Your-Hands Year (Steady), where what pushes you forward and what holds you back are about even. You might find one person to start with and promise to cheer on each other's first steps.

rows.ko: 다가오는 해는 새로운 시작을 위한 땅을 고르는, 기반을 다지는 해(역풍)예요. {{근거}} 시기라 무언가를 시작하려 할 때 갖춰야 할 조건과 책임이 먼저 눈에 들어오기 쉽습니다. 시작하려는 일을 작은 규모로 미리 연습해 보는 ‘시험 운행’을 한 번 해 보세요. 이 해에 다진 준비와 연습은 새로운 시작이 오래 이어지도록 받쳐 주는 주춧돌이 됩니다.
rows.en: The coming year is a Building Year, a season for preparing the ground where your new start will grow. With {{근거}}, requirements and responsibilities catch your eye first whenever you try to begin. Do a ‘test run’: practice what you want to start on a small scale. The prep and practice you put in this year become the cornerstone that makes your new start last.
rows.en_before_tone: The coming year is a Groundwork Year (Headwind), a time to prepare the ground for a new start. With {{근거}}, when you try to start something, the conditions and responsibilities you need to meet may catch your eye first. Try a ‘test run’: practice what you want to start on a small scale first. The preparation and practice you build this year become the cornerstone that helps your new start last.

rows.ko: {{근거}} 때라, 다가오는 해는 새로운 시작이 생각보다 더디게 움직이는 기반을 다지는 해(역풍)입니다. 첫발을 떼려 할 때마다 넘어야 할 문턱이 하나씩 나타나 지치기 쉬워요. 그럴수록 시작의 크기를 줄여, 오늘 할 수 있는 가장 작은 준비 하나에 집중해 보세요. 문턱을 하나씩 넘으며 얻은 끈기는 출발 뒤의 긴 길을 견디게 하는 힘으로 남습니다.
rows.en: With {{근거}} in play, the coming year is a Building Year, and your new start moves slower than you hoped. Each time you reach for the first step, another hurdle appears, and that wears on you. All the more reason to shrink your start and focus on the smallest bit of prep you can do today. The grit you build clearing each hurdle carries you down the long road once you're on your way.
rows.en_before_tone: With {{근거}}, the coming year is a Groundwork Year (Headwind), when a new start may move more slowly than expected. Each time you try to take the first step, another threshold may appear, which can wear you out. That's all the more reason to make your start smaller and focus on the smallest bit of preparation you can do today. The persistence you gain crossing each threshold remains as the strength to keep going on the long road after you set out.

rows.ko: 새로운 시작을 꿈꾸는 당신에게 다가오는 해는 출발선 앞에서 숨을 고르는, 기반을 다지는 해(역풍)예요. {{근거}} 시기라 지금 맡은 일을 마무리하는 책임이 무겁게 남아 새 일을 벌이기 쉽지 않을 수 있습니다. 끝내지 못한 일 하나를 골라 이 해 안에 깔끔하게 마무리해 보세요. 잘 끝맺은 경험은 다음 시작을 가볍고 단단하게 만들어 주는 바탕이 되어 줘요.
rows.en: Your dream of a fresh start meets a Building Year in the coming year, a time to catch your breath at the starting line. As {{근거}} leaves you carrying the weight of finishing what's already on your plate, launching something new takes extra effort. Choose one loose end and tie it up neatly before the year is out. Finishing well makes your next start lighter and steadier.
rows.en_before_tone: If you've been dreaming of a new start, the coming year is a Groundwork Year (Headwind), a time to catch your breath at the starting line. With {{근거}}, the responsibility of finishing your current work may weigh on you, making it hard to begin something new. You might choose one unfinished task and wrap it up neatly within this year. The experience of finishing well becomes a base that makes your next start lighter and steadier.

rows.ko: 솔직하게 말하면 다가오는 해는 새로운 시작이 단번에 열리는 해는 아니에요. {{근거}} 때라 시작에 따르는 조건을 하나하나 확인하고 채워야 하는, 기반을 다지는 해(역풍)입니다. 시작하려는 분야의 사람들과 미리 이야기를 나누며 현실적인 정보를 모아 보세요. 이 시기에 모은 정보와 관계는 막상 출발할 때 길을 잃지 않게 해 주는 지도가 되어 줍니다.
rows.en: Let's be honest: the coming year doesn't simply fling open the door to a new start. Because of {{근거}}, it's a Building Year, when you check off the conditions for starting one by one. Talk with people already in the field you want to enter, and gather real-world information ahead of time. The knowledge and connections you gather now become a map that keeps you on course once you set out.
rows.en_before_tone: To be honest, the coming year isn't one where a new start opens all at once. With {{근거}}, it's a Groundwork Year (Headwind), when you need to check and fill the conditions for starting one by one. It can help to talk with people in the field you want to enter and gather realistic information ahead of time. The information and relationships you gather now become a map that keeps you from getting lost when you finally set out.

rows.ko: 바라던 새로운 시작은 {{열리는해}}에 가장 힘차게 문을 열기 쉬워요. {{근거}} 흐름이라 그해에는 낯선 일과 배움에 뛰어들기 좋습니다. 그때까지 관심 가는 분야의 짧은 체험을 틈틈이 해 두면, 그해에 어떤 길을 고를지 분명해져요.
rows.en: The fresh start you've hoped for swings its door wide open in {{열리는해}}. With {{근거}}, that year invites you to dive into new kinds of work and learning. Until then, give the fields that interest you a quick test drive, so you know which path to choose when that year comes.
rows.en_before_tone: The new start you've hoped for is most likely to swing its door open in {{열리는해}}. With {{근거}}, that year is a good time to dive into unfamiliar work and learning. Until then, if you try short taste-tests in fields that interest you, it will become clear which path to choose that year.

rows.ko: {{근거}} 시기인 {{열리는해}}에는 오래 품어 온 계획을 실행에 옮기기 한층 수월해집니다. 그해에는 새로운 곳, 새로운 사람, 새로운 역할에 마음을 열어 두기 좋아요. 그 전까지 지금 하는 일 가운데 정리할 것과 이어 갈 것을 나눠 두면 새 출발이 한결 가벼워질 수 있어요.
rows.en: {{열리는해}}, with {{근거}}, makes it far easier to turn long-held plans into action. That year, open yourself to new places, new people, and new roles. Before then, sort what you're doing now into what to wrap up and what to keep, and your fresh start will feel much lighter.
rows.en_before_tone: In {{열리는해}}, a time of {{근거}}, it becomes much easier to put long-held plans into action. That year is a good time to keep your heart open to new places, new people, and new roles. Before then, if you sort what you're doing now into what to wrap up and what to keep, your fresh start can feel much lighter.

rows.ko: {{열리는해}}에 이르면 {{근거}} 덕분에 새로운 시작 앞의 망설임이 한결 옅어지기 쉽습니다. 그해에는 처음 해 보는 일을 작게라도 직접 시작해 보기 좋아요. 그때를 기다리며 시작에 필요한 시간과 비용을 조금씩 마련해 두세요.
rows.en: By {{열리는해}}, {{근거}} melts away your doubts about a new start. That year, begin something new for real, even if it's small. In the meantime, start setting aside the time and money you'll need to get going.
rows.en_before_tone: When {{열리는해}} arrives, thanks to {{근거}}, hesitation about a new start is likely to fade. That year is a good time to actually begin something new, even on a small scale. While you wait, it helps to gradually set aside the time and money you'll need to get started.

rows.ko: 앞으로의 다섯 해 가운데 {{열리는해}}에는 새로운 시작을 위한 문이 가장 넓게 열립니다. {{근거}} 때라 그해에는 익숙한 자리를 벗어나 한 걸음 나아가기 좋아요. 그 전까지 작은 처음을 자주 경험해 두면, 그해의 큰 시작도 덜 낯설게 맞을 수 있습니다.
rows.en: {{열리는해}} is the year, out of the next five, when the door to a new start opens widest. Thanks to {{근거}}, that year is made for stepping out of your comfort zone and moving forward. Before then, collect plenty of small firsts, so that year's big leap feels less like stepping into the unknown.
rows.en_before_tone: Of the next five years, {{열리는해}} is when the door to a new start opens widest. With {{근거}}, that year is a good time to step out of familiar places and move forward. Before then, if you often experience small firsts, that year's big start can feel less unfamiliar.

rows.ko: 다섯 해 안에 새로운 시작이 활짝 열리는 해는 따로 보이지 않아, 하늘의 바람보다 작은 시도를 거듭하는 용기가 출발을 정하는 시기예요. {{가까운해}}에는 흐름이 조금 더 새로운 시작 쪽으로 기우니, 그때까지 한 계절에 한 번씩 낯선 경험을 해 보면 좋습니다.
rows.en: Across the next five years, no year opens wide for a new start, so your courage to keep trying small things, not the winds overhead, decides when you set out. Things lean a little toward new beginnings in {{가까운해}}. Until then, try something unfamiliar once a season.
rows.en_before_tone: No year in the next five stands out as a Wide-Open Year for a new start, so the courage to keep trying small things, more than any wind from the sky, decides when you set out. In {{가까운해}}, the flow tilts a little more toward new starts, so until then it helps to try something unfamiliar once a season.

rows.ko: {{가까운해}}에 새로운 시작이 가장 가까워지지만, 다섯 해 안에 크게 열리는 순풍의 해는 뚜렷하지 않습니다. 그래서 거창한 출발보다 작게 시작해 꾸준히 이어 가는 방식이 새로운 시작을 오래 지켜 줘요.
rows.en: {{가까운해}} brings a new start closest, though no clear Open Year appears in the next five. So instead of a grand launch, start small and keep it going. That's what protects a fresh start over the long run.
rows.en_before_tone: A new start comes closest in {{가까운해}}, but no tailwind year opens wide within the next five. So rather than a grand departure, starting small and keeping it going protects your new start for the long run.

rows.ko: 이어질 다섯 해는 순풍을 기다리기보다 출발에 필요한 준비를 한 칸씩 채워 가는 시기입니다. {{가까운해}}에 새로운 시작의 흐름이 가장 순해지니, 그때까지 시작에 필요한 기술 하나를 정해 꾸준히 익혀 가 보세요.
rows.en: For the next five years, fill in the prep you need one step at a time instead of waiting for a tailwind. New beginnings come most easily in {{가까운해}}, so until then, choose one skill you'll need to get started and keep honing it.
rows.en_before_tone: The next five years are a time to fill in the preparation you need, one step at a time, rather than wait for a tailwind. The flow of new starts is gentlest in {{가까운해}}, so until then, you might pick one skill you'll need to begin and keep learning it.

rows.ko: 다섯 해를 내다봐도 새로운 시작에 순풍이 크게 부는 해는 보이지 않아, 스스로 문을 여는 힘이 더 중요해요. {{가까운해}}에는 그 문이 한결 가볍게 열리기 쉬우니, 하던 일 가운데 마무리할 것을 미리 정리해 두면 좋습니다.
rows.en: No strong tailwind for a new start appears anywhere in the next five years, so your power to open the door yourself matters most. That door swings open more easily in {{가까운해}}. Get ready now: decide which of your current projects to wrap up first.
rows.en_before_tone: Looking ahead five years, no year shows a strong tailwind for a new start, so the strength to open the door yourself matters more. In {{가까운해}}, that door is likely to open more easily, so it helps to sort out ahead of time which of your current tasks to wrap up.

rows.en: Write 'what I handled solo' beside 'what I could have asked for'
rows.en_before_tone: Write 'what I did alone' and 'what I could have asked for help with' side by side

rows.ko: 이번 주 혼자 힘으로 해낸 업무 하나와, 혼자 짊어졌지만 사실 부탁해도 됐던 업무 하나를 나란히 적어 보세요. 뒤의 것에는 다음에 부탁할 동료 이름과 그에게 건넬 한 문장을 덧붙여 둡니다.
rows.en: Write down two tasks from this week side by side: one you handled on your own, and one you carried alone that you could easily have shared. Beside the second, add the name of a coworker you'll ask next time and the one sentence you'll say to them.
rows.en_before_tone: Try writing down, side by side, one task you handled on your own this week and one task you carried alone that you actually could have asked for help with. Next to the second one, add the name of a coworker you'll ask next time and one sentence you'll say to them.

rows.ko: 모두 기대거나 혼자 다 짊어지면 어느 쪽이든 지치기 쉽습니다. 해낸 것은 인정하고 부탁할 것은 미리 챙겨 두면 기대는 문턱이 낮아져요.
rows.en: Leaning on others for everything wears you out, and so does carrying it all yourself. Credit yourself for what you've done, plan what to ask for, and reaching out stops feeling like a leap.
rows.en_before_tone: Leaning on others for everything and carrying everything alone are both exhausting. When you acknowledge what you've done and plan ahead for what to ask, leaning on others feels less daunting.

rows.ko: 모르는 것을 인정하고 도움을 청해보기
rows.en: Admit what you don't know, and ask
rows.en_before_tone: Admit what you don't know and ask for help

rows.ko: 오늘 업무 중 막히는 것 하나를 혼자 오래 붙잡기 전에 아는 동료에게 짧게 물어보세요. 사소한 질문일수록 연습으로는 더 좋습니다.
rows.en: When you hit a wall at work today, don't wrestle with it alone for ages. Ask a coworker a quick question. The smaller the question, the better the practice.
rows.en_before_tone: When you get stuck on something at work today, try asking a coworker you know a quick question before wrestling with it alone for too long. The smaller the question, the better the practice.

rows.ko: 작게 물어본 경험이 쌓이면 '물어봐도 괜찮다'는 감각이 생깁니다. 큰 도움을 청할 때의 부담도 그만큼 줄어들어요.
rows.en: Every small question teaches you that asking is safe. As that sense grows, asking for bigger help feels lighter, too.
rows.en_before_tone: As small questions add up, you develop a sense that 'it's okay to ask.' The pressure of asking for bigger help shrinks along with it.

rows.ko: 재직 중일 때
rows.en: If you're currently working
rows.note: 재직 중일 때 → 'If you're currently working'로 통일

rows.ko: 혼자 끌어안지 않고 가볍게 이야기해보기
rows.en: Don't bottle it up: say it out loud
rows.en_before_tone: Instead of holding it in, mention it lightly

rows.ko: 요즘 일 때문에 마음이 무거웠다면 편한 동료나 친구에게 '요즘 이 일이 좀 버거워' 정도로만 꺼내 보세요. 해결책을 듣지 않아도 괜찮습니다.
rows.en: If work has been weighing on you, tell a coworker or friend you trust something simple, like 'This job has been a lot lately.' You don't need them to fix anything.
rows.en_before_tone: If work has been weighing on you lately, try saying something as simple as 'this has been a bit much lately' to a coworker or friend you're comfortable with. You don't need to hear a solution.

rows.ko: 힘든 마음은 말로 나누기만 해도 무게가 조금 덜어집니다. 기댈 사람이 곁에 있다는 걸 확인하는 시간이기도 해요.
rows.en: Putting a heavy feeling into words lightens its weight. It also reminds you that someone stands beside you, ready to be leaned on.
rows.en_before_tone: Just putting a hard feeling into words and sharing it can lighten the load a little. It's also a chance to confirm you have someone to lean on.

rows.ko: 재직 중일 때
rows.en: If you're currently working

rows.ko: 막히는 일을 '방법을 몰라서 / 불안해서'로 나눠 보기
rows.en: Sort what's blocking you: 'don't know how' or 'feeling anxious'
rows.en_before_tone: Sort where you're stuck into 'don't know how' and 'feeling anxious'

rows.ko: 준비 중인 공부나 계획에서 막히는 일 하나를 골라 '방법을 안다면 해 볼까?' 하고 스스로 물어보세요. 방법을 몰라서라면 물어볼 사람이나 자료를 하나 적고, 불안해서라면 그때 속으로 한 말을 한 줄 적습니다.
rows.en: Pick one place you're stuck in your studies or plans, and ask yourself: 'If I knew how, would I do it?' If the answer is not knowing how, write down one person or resource to ask. If it's anxiety, write one line about what you told yourself in that moment.
rows.en_before_tone: Try picking one place you're stuck in your studies or plans, and ask yourself, 'If I knew how, would I try it?' If it's because you don't know how, write down one person or resource to ask; if it's anxiety, write down in one line what you said to yourself in that moment.

rows.ko: 막힘이 내가 모자라서가 아니라 배우면 되는 문제일 때가 많아요. 무엇이 필요한지 가려지면 누구에게 기댈지도 선명해집니다.
rows.en: Being stuck rarely means you're not good enough. Usually it just means there's something left to learn. Once you name what you need, you see exactly who to turn to.
rows.en_before_tone: Often, being stuck isn't because you're lacking but because it's something you can learn. Once you see what you need, it becomes clearer who to lean on.

rows.ko: 기준은 높아도 여유 있는 사람에게 하루 시간 배분 물어보기
rows.en: Ask someone with high standards and an easy calm how they spend their day
rows.en_before_tone: Ask someone with high standards but plenty of ease how they divide their day

rows.ko: 자기 일을 잘하면서도 삶을 즐기는 것 같은 사람 한 명에게 공부·일·쉼·잠에 하루를 어떻게 나눠 쓰는지 가볍게 물어보세요. 내 하루와 나란히 적어 보고, 가장 다른 칸 하나만 조금 옮겨 봅니다.
rows.en: Find one person who excels at their work yet clearly enjoys life, and casually ask how they divide their day among study, work, downtime, and sleep. Write their day next to yours, then shift just the one block that differs most.
rows.en_before_tone: Try casually asking one person who seems good at what they do and still enjoys life how they split their day between study, work, rest, and sleep. Write it next to your own day, then shift just the one slot that differs most, a little.

rows.ko: 내 기준이 적당한지는 혼자 가늠하기 어렵습니다. 그대로 따라 하지 않고 참고만 해도 균형을 찾는 데 도움을 받을 수 있어요.
rows.en: You can't always judge your own standards from the inside, so borrow another set of eyes. Use their day as a reference point, not a template, and you'll find your balance faster.
rows.en_before_tone: It's hard to judge alone whether your standards are reasonable. Even using someone's day just as a reference, without copying it, can help you find balance.

rows.ko: '쉬면 안 될 이유'를 적고 잠깐 쉬어보기
rows.en: List your 'reasons I can't rest,' then rest anyway
rows.en_before_tone: Write down 'reasons I can't rest,' then rest for a moment

rows.ko: 공부나 준비 때문에 쉬지 못한 순간을 떠올려 '쉬면 안 될 이유'를 적은 뒤, 잠깐 쉬어도 되는 때를 정해 실제로 쉬어 보세요. 쉬는 동안 떠오르는 생각에는 '할 일 생각이네' 하고 이름만 붙여 둡니다.
rows.en: Recall a moment when studying or prep kept you from resting, and write down your 'reasons I can't rest.' Then choose a time when a short break is fine, and take it for real. When thoughts pop up as you rest, simply label them 'to-do thoughts' and let them drift by.
rows.en_before_tone: Try recalling a moment you couldn't rest because of studying or preparing, write down your 'reasons I can't rest,' then pick a time when a short break is okay and actually take it. If thoughts come up while you rest, just label them: 'that's a to-do thought.'

rows.ko: 혼자 다 해내려는 마음은 쉼마저 미루게 만들어요. 쉬는 데 시간을 내어 주는 것도 나에게 기대는 연습입니다.
rows.en: Trying to do it all yourself pushes even rest off the list. Giving yourself time to rest is how you practice leaning on yourself.
rows.en_before_tone: Wanting to do everything yourself can make you put off even rest. Making time to rest is also practice in leaning on yourself.

rows.ko: '따뜻함·이해·든든함' 세 칸에 바라는 것 한 줄씩 쓰기
rows.en: Write one line each for warmth, understanding, and support
rows.en_before_tone: Write one line each under 'warmth, understanding, support'

rows.ko: 안아 주고 관심 가져 주기, 들어 주고 알아주기, 힘을 실어 주기 세 칸에 요즘 연애에서 '이렇게 해 주면 좋겠다'를 한 줄씩 적어 보세요. 그중 하나를 골라 상대나 가까운 사람에게 건넬 문장으로 바꿔 봅니다.
rows.en: Make three columns: hugs and attention, listening and understanding, and having your back. In each, write one line about what you'd love from your relationship right now. Then choose one and turn it into words you can actually say to your partner or someone close.
rows.en_before_tone: Under three headings (hugs and attention, listening and understanding, and backing you up), try writing one line each about what you'd like in your love life right now. Then pick one and turn it into a sentence you could say to your partner or someone close.

rows.ko: 받고 싶은 것이 따뜻함인지 이해인지 든든함인지 이름이 붙으면 청할 방향이 생깁니다. 막연한 서운함보다 훨씬 전하기 쉬워요.
rows.en: Once you can name whether you crave warmth, understanding, or support, you know exactly what to ask for. A named need is far easier to voice than a vague sense of being let down.
rows.en_before_tone: Once you name whether what you want is warmth, understanding, or support, you know what to ask for. It's much easier to express than a vague sense of hurt.

rows.ko: 외로울 때 '연결이 필요하구나' 적고 작은 연결 하나 하기
rows.en: Feeling lonely? Write 'I need connection,' then reach out in one small way
rows.en_before_tone: When lonely, write 'I need connection' and make one small connection

rows.ko: 외로움이나 허전함이 올라오면 '지금 나는 연결이 필요하구나'라고 한 줄 적고, 그 마음을 탓하지 않는 문장 하나를 나에게 건네 보세요. 그다음 안부 메시지 한 통처럼 오늘 할 수 있는 작은 연결 하나를 해 봅니다.
rows.en: When loneliness or emptiness creeps in, write one line: 'Right now, I need connection.' Then offer yourself one kind sentence that doesn't judge the feeling. After that, make one small connection you can manage today, like texting someone to see how they're doing.
rows.en_before_tone: When loneliness or emptiness rises up, try writing one line, 'Right now I need connection,' and offering yourself a sentence that doesn't blame that feeling. Then make one small connection you can manage today, like sending a message to check in on someone.

rows.ko: 외로움은 부족함이 아니라 연결이 필요하다는 신호입니다. 그 마음을 인정하고 작게 채우면 기대는 힘도 조금씩 자라요.
rows.en: Loneliness isn't a flaw. It's a signal that you need connection. Acknowledge it, answer it in small ways, and your ability to lean on others grows steadily.
rows.en_before_tone: Loneliness isn't a flaw; it's a signal that you need connection. When you acknowledge it and meet it in small ways, your ability to lean on others grows little by little.

rows.ko: 각자 선호하는 응원 표현 알아보기
rows.en: Discover how each of you likes to be supported
rows.en_before_tone: Learn each other's preferred ways of being encouraged

rows.ko: 힘든 날 어떤 말이 부담스럽고 어떤 말이 도움이 되는지 연인과 서로 하나씩 알려 주세요. 서로의 답을 메모해 두면 다음에 꺼내 쓰기 좋습니다.
rows.en: Take turns telling your partner one thing that feels like pressure on a rough day and one thing that truly helps. Jot down each other's answers so they're ready when you need them.
rows.en_before_tone: Try sharing with your partner one thing each that feels like pressure on a hard day and one thing that actually helps. Jotting down each other's answers makes them easy to use next time.

rows.ko: 응원도 사람마다 와닿는 말이 다릅니다. 나에게 맞는 위로를 미리 알려 두면 힘든 날 기대기가 한결 수월해져요.
rows.en: Encouragement lands differently for everyone. Tell your partner ahead of time what comforts you, and leaning on them on a hard day becomes so much easier.
rows.en_before_tone: Different words of encouragement land differently for different people. Letting someone know ahead of time what comforts you makes leaning on them on hard days much easier.

rows.ko: 연인이 있을 때
rows.en: If you're in a relationship
rows.note: 연인이 있을 때 → 'If you're in a relationship'로 통일

rows.ko: 내 곁의 사람 지도를 그리고 마음 쓰이는 한 명에 별표하기
rows.en: Map the people around you and star the one on your mind
rows.en_before_tone: Draw a map of the people around you and star one you're thinking about

rows.ko: 가족을 중심으로 떠오르는 사람들을 적고, 얼마나 가까운지, 기댈 수 있는지, 불편한 말도 할 수 있는지 표시해 보세요. 요즘 가장 마음에 걸리는 한 사람에게만 별표를 달면 충분합니다.
rows.en: Starting with family, write down the people who come to mind. Beside each, note how close you are, whether you can lean on them, and whether you can raise hard topics with them. Then star just the one person who's been on your mind most lately.
rows.en_before_tone: Starting with family, try writing down the people who come to mind and marking how close they are, whether you can lean on them, and whether you can say uncomfortable things to them. It's enough to put a star by just the one person on your mind most lately.

rows.ko: 곁의 사람들을 한 장에 그려 보면 지금 기대는 사람과 더 가까워지고 싶은 사람이 함께 보여요. 떠오르는 사람이 적어도 괜찮습니다.
rows.en: Putting everyone on one page shows you who you lean on now and who you want to draw closer to. A short list is perfectly fine.
rows.en_before_tone: Drawing the people around you on one page shows both who you lean on now and who you'd like to be closer to. It's okay if only a few people come to mind.

rows.ko: 혼자 안고 있지 않고 가볍게 이야기부터 꺼내기
rows.en: Don't carry it alone: start by mentioning it lightly
rows.en_before_tone: Instead of holding it alone, start by bringing it up lightly

rows.ko: 가족 일로 혼자 고민하던 것이 있다면 편한 가족 한 사람에게 '요즘 이게 좀 마음에 걸려' 정도로만 꺼내 보세요. 답을 정해 두지 않고 이야기를 여는 것까지가 목표입니다.
rows.en: If you've been worrying over a family matter alone, mention it to one family member you feel at ease with, something like 'This has been on my mind lately.' You don't need an answer ready. Your only goal is to open the conversation.
rows.en_before_tone: If there's a family matter you've been worrying about alone, try mentioning it to one family member you're comfortable with, just as 'this has been on my mind lately.' The goal is simply to open the conversation, without deciding on an answer first.

rows.ko: 가족 사이일수록 걱정을 끼칠까 봐 혼자 안고 있기 쉽습니다. 가볍게 꺼내 보면 기대도 되는 사이라는 것을 확인할 수 있어요.
rows.en: With family especially, you tend to keep worries to yourself so no one else frets. Bring it up lightly, and you discover this is a bond you can truly lean on.
rows.en_before_tone: With family especially, it's easy to keep worries to yourself so you don't burden them. Bringing it up lightly can show you that this is a relationship you can lean on.

rows.ko: 함께한 기억 한 장면 전하기
rows.en: Share one memory you made together

rows.ko: 가족과 함께했던 좋은 기억 하나가 떠오르면 짧은 메시지로 전해 보세요. 사진 한 장을 곁들여도 좋습니다.
rows.en: When a happy memory with your family surfaces, send it to them in a short message. Add a photo for a warm touch.
rows.en_before_tone: When a good memory with your family comes to mind, try sharing it in a short message. Adding a photo is nice too.

rows.ko: 좋았던 장면을 함께 떠올리면 부탁이나 용건 없이도 마음이 가까워져요. 이런 연결이 쌓여 있어야 힘들 때 기대기도 쉬워집니다.
rows.en: Revisiting good times together draws you closer, even when no one needs anything. Moments like these build up and make leaning on each other easier when life gets hard.
rows.en_before_tone: Recalling good moments together brings hearts closer even without a favor or errand. When these connections build up, it's easier to lean on each other in hard times.

rows.ko: 힘들 때 기댈 곳과 응원받을 곳을 한 장에 적기
rows.en: On one page, map where you turn on hard days and who cheers you on
rows.en_before_tone: On one page, write down where you can lean when things are hard and where you get cheered on

rows.ko: 가운데 나를 적고, 힘든 날 연락하면 마음이 놓이는 친구, 새로운 걸 해 볼 때 응원해 줄 사람, 사람이 아니어도 마음이 놓이는 곳을 둘레에 적어 보세요. 빈칸은 앞으로 채워 갈 자리로 남겨 두면 됩니다.
rows.en: Write your name in the center. Around it, add a friend who's easy to call on a rough day, someone who'd cheer you on when you try something new, and places (not only people) that settle your mind. Leave any blank spots open for the future to fill.
rows.en_before_tone: Try writing yourself in the middle, and around you, a friend who puts you at ease when you reach out on a hard day, someone who'd cheer you on when you try something new, and places (not just people) that calm you. Any blanks can stay as spaces to fill in later.

rows.ko: 든든한 사람이 있으면 더 잘 쉬고 더 멀리 가 볼 수 있습니다. 기댈 곳을 눈으로 확인해 두면 연락할 용기도 생겨요.
rows.en: With people you can count on, you rest more deeply and venture further. Seeing your support network on paper gives you the courage to reach out.
rows.en_before_tone: Having people you can rely on helps you rest better and venture further. Seeing where you can lean also gives you the courage to reach out.

rows.ko: 혼자 끌어안지 않고 힘들다는 것부터 주변에 알리기
rows.en: Don't keep it in: start by saying you're struggling
rows.en_before_tone: Instead of holding it in, start by letting people know you're struggling

rows.ko: 요즘 힘든 일이 있다면 해결을 부탁하기 전에 믿을 만한 친구에게 '나 요즘 좀 힘들어' 하고 지금 상태부터 알려 보세요. 길게 설명하지 않아도 괜찮습니다.
rows.en: If something's been hard lately, don't jump straight to asking anyone to fix it. First tell a friend you trust where you are: 'I've been having a rough time lately.' No long explanation needed.
rows.en_before_tone: If something's been hard lately, before asking anyone to fix it, try starting by telling a trusted friend how you are: 'I've been having a hard time lately.' You don't need to explain at length.

rows.ko: 도움을 청하는 첫걸음은 힘들다는 걸 알리는 일입니다. 알고 있는 사람이 한 명만 있어도 마음이 덜 외로워져요.
rows.en: Asking for help starts with letting someone know you're having a hard time. Even one person knowing makes you feel far less alone.
rows.en_before_tone: The first step in asking for help is letting someone know you're struggling. Even one person knowing can make you feel less alone.

rows.ko: 답장을 재촉하지 않는 안부 보내기
rows.en: Send a check-in that asks for no reply
rows.en_before_tone: Send a check-in that doesn't press for a reply

rows.ko: 오랜만에 떠오른 친구에게 '답장은 편할 때 해도 돼'라는 말과 함께 가벼운 안부를 보내 보세요. 답이 늦어도 기다리지 않는 것이 이 실천의 약속입니다.
rows.en: Send a light hello to a friend who's crossed your mind after a long while, and add 'Reply whenever it suits you.' Your promise in this practice: don't wait on the answer, however long it takes.
rows.en_before_tone: Try sending a light hello to a friend who's come to mind after a while, with 'reply whenever it suits you.' The one promise here is not to wait on a reply, even if it's slow.

rows.ko: 부담 없는 안부는 관계의 끈을 느슨하게라도 이어 줍니다. 그 끈이 있어야 필요할 때 기대기도 편해요.
rows.en: A no-pressure check-in keeps the thread of a friendship intact, even loosely. With that thread in place, leaning on each other comes easily when you need it.
rows.en_before_tone: A no-pressure check-in keeps the thread of a relationship going, even loosely. With that thread in place, it's easier to lean on each other when you need to.

rows.ko: 누군가에게 말하기 전, 글로 상태를 정리해보기
rows.en: Before you talk to anyone, put your situation on paper
rows.en_before_tone: Before telling anyone, sort out your situation in writing

rows.ko: 돈이나 생활 문제로 마음이 무거울 때, 누군가에게 말하기 전에 지금 걱정되는 것과 필요한 도움을 글로 적어 보세요. 정리가 덜 돼도 떠오르는 대로 쓰면 됩니다.
rows.en: When money or everyday worries weigh on you, write down what worries you and what help you need before you talk to anyone. Skip the polish. Just write whatever comes to mind.
rows.en_before_tone: When money or everyday worries weigh on you, before talking to anyone, try writing down what you're worried about and what help you need. It's fine if it's not organized; just write what comes to mind.

rows.ko: 돈 걱정은 막연할수록 꺼내기 어렵습니다. 글로 먼저 정리해 두면 무엇을 누구에게 물어볼지가 보여요.
rows.en: The fuzzier a money worry, the harder it is to raise. Put it on paper first, and you'll see what to ask for and who to ask.
rows.en_before_tone: The vaguer a money worry is, the harder it is to bring up. Sorting it out in writing first shows you what to ask and whom.

rows.ko: 당사자가 아닌 사람에게 객관적 의견을 구해보기
rows.en: Get an outside view from someone who isn't involved
rows.en_before_tone: Ask someone not directly involved for an objective view

rows.ko: 지출이나 생활비 고민 하나를 골라, 그 일과 직접 얽히지 않은 믿을 만한 사람에게 의견을 물어보세요. '너라면 어떻게 하겠어?' 한마디면 충분합니다.
rows.en: Choose one worry about spending or living costs and ask a trusted person who isn't directly involved for their take. A simple 'What would you do?' is all it takes.
rows.en_before_tone: Try picking one worry about spending or living costs, and asking a trusted person who isn't directly tied to it for their opinion. 'What would you do?' is enough.

rows.ko: 혼자 계산하면 걱정이 커지기 쉽지만 바깥의 눈은 의외로 담백한 답을 줄 때가 있어요. 생활 문제도 기대어 풀 수 있다는 감각이 생깁니다.
rows.en: Running the numbers alone makes worries snowball, but a fresh pair of eyes often spots a surprisingly simple answer. You learn that even everyday problems ease when you lean on someone.
rows.en_before_tone: Calculating alone can make worries grow, but an outside eye sometimes gives a surprisingly simple answer. You'll get a sense that even everyday problems can be solved by leaning on others.

rows.ko: 잠깐 숨을 천천히 늦춰보기
rows.en: Slow your breathing for a moment

rows.ko: 통장이나 카드 내역을 열기 전, 등을 의자에 기대고 들숨과 날숨을 천천히 늦춰 잠깐 쉬어 보세요. 잘 안 느려져도 괜찮으니 숨이 오가는 감각에만 살짝 주의를 둡니다.
rows.en: Before you open your bank or card statement, lean back in your chair and pause to slow your breathing. If it won't slow much, that's fine. Simply rest your attention on each breath coming and going.
rows.en_before_tone: Before opening your bank or card statement, try leaning back in your chair and slowing your inhales and exhales for a short pause. It's okay if it doesn't slow down much; just rest your attention lightly on the feeling of breath coming and going.

rows.ko: 몸이 긴장하면 숫자도 더 무섭게 보이기 쉽습니다. 숨을 늦추는 것만으로도 마음이 조금 가라앉아 차분히 볼 수 있어요.
rows.en: A tense body makes numbers look scarier than they are. Slowing your breath settles your mind enough to look at them calmly.
rows.en_before_tone: When your body is tense, numbers can look scarier. Simply slowing your breath can settle your mind a little so you can look calmly.

rows.ko: 당장 해결하려 하지 않고 '걱정이 남아 있구나' 적어두기
rows.en: Don't solve it tonight: just note 'this worry is still here'
rows.en_before_tone: Rather than solving it right now, note 'this worry is still here'

rows.ko: 퇴근 무렵까지 마음에 남은 업무 걱정은 억지로 지금 해결하려 하지 말고 '이 걱정이 아직 남아 있구나' 하고 짧게 적어 두세요. 그리고 다시 확인할 시간만 정해 둡니다.
rows.en: If a work worry is still on your mind at the end of the day, don't force a solution now. Simply jot down, 'This worry is still here.' Then set a time to come back to it.
rows.en_before_tone: If a work worry is still on your mind near the end of the day, there's no need to force yourself to solve it now; try simply jotting down, 'this worry is still here.' Then just set a time to check on it again.

rows.ko: 감정에 이름을 붙이면 그 감정과 조금 거리가 생깁니다. 확인할 때를 정해 두면 그 전까지는 마음을 놓아도 돼요.
rows.en: Naming a feeling puts distance between you and it. Once you've set a time to check back, your mind is free to rest until then.
rows.en_before_tone: Naming a feeling creates a little distance from it. Once you've set a time to check, you can let your mind rest until then.

rows.ko: 재직 중일 때
rows.en: If you're currently working

rows.ko: 미완료 업무에 다음 행동 표시하기
rows.en: Mark the next step on anything unfinished
rows.en_before_tone: Mark the next step on unfinished tasks

rows.ko: 오늘 끝내지 못한 일에는 내일 가장 먼저 할 행동 하나만 적어 두세요. '자료 열어 보기'처럼 작을수록 좋습니다.
rows.en: For anything you didn't wrap up today, write down the single first thing to do tomorrow. Keep it tiny, like 'open the file.'
rows.en_before_tone: For anything you didn't finish today, try writing down just one action to do first tomorrow. The smaller the better, like 'open the file.'

rows.ko: 끝내지 못한 일은 머릿속에 계속 맴돌기 쉬워요. 다음 걸음을 적어 두면 머리가 그 일을 잠시 내려놓을 수 있습니다.
rows.en: Unfinished tasks love to loop in your head. Write down the next step, and your mind can set that task down for a while.
rows.en_before_tone: Unfinished tasks tend to keep circling in your head. Writing down the next step lets your mind set that task down for a while.

rows.ko: 재직 중일 때
rows.en: If you're currently working

rows.ko: 목, 어깨 등 뭉친 부위를 짧게 풀어주기
rows.en: Release tight spots like your neck and shoulders
rows.en_before_tone: Briefly loosen tight spots like your neck and shoulders

rows.ko: 일하다 긴장이 느껴질 때 어깨를 귀 쪽으로 올렸다가 툭 떨어뜨리고, 목을 천천히 좌우로 기울여 보세요. 자리에서 잠깐이면 충분합니다.
rows.en: When tension creeps in at work, lift your shoulders toward your ears and let them drop, then slowly tilt your head from side to side. A few moments at your desk is enough.
rows.en_before_tone: When you notice tension while working, try lifting your shoulders toward your ears and letting them drop, then slowly tilting your neck side to side. A moment at your desk is enough.

rows.ko: 걱정이 많을 때 몸은 먼저 굳어 있곤 합니다. 몸의 긴장을 풀어 주면 마음도 함께 한숨 돌릴 수 있어요.
rows.en: Worry often lands in your body before you notice it. Release that physical tension, and your mind catches its breath too.
rows.en_before_tone: When you're worried, your body often tightens up first. Releasing physical tension lets your mind catch its breath too.

rows.ko: 재직 중일 때
rows.en: If you're currently working

rows.ko: 막막한 일과 예전에 해낸 일을 한 줄로 잇기
rows.en: Link something daunting to something you've already done, in one line
rows.en_before_tone: Link something daunting to something you've done before, in one line

rows.ko: 앞두고 막막한 준비 하나를 적고, 예전에 비슷하게 어려웠지만 결국 해낸 일과 그때 쓴 방법을 적어 보세요. 이번에 실제로 쓸 수 있는 부분 하나만 골라 둡니다.
rows.en: Write down one daunting thing you're preparing for. Then write something from your past that felt just as hard but that you got through, and how you did it. Choose one piece of that approach to use this time.
rows.en_before_tone: Try writing down one daunting thing you're preparing for, then something from the past that was similarly hard but you eventually managed, and the method you used. Then pick just one part you can actually use this time.

rows.ko: 이번 일이 낯설게만 느껴져도 예전에 해낸 일과 닮은 데가 있어요. 해낸 경험을 떠올리면 나를 믿을 근거가 생깁니다.
rows.en: Even what feels brand new shares something with challenges you've already met. Remembering what you've pulled off gives you solid ground for trusting yourself.
rows.en_before_tone: Even if this feels completely unfamiliar, it has something in common with things you've done before. Remembering what you've accomplished gives you a reason to trust yourself.

rows.ko: 해낼 수 있겠다 싶을 만큼 계획 크기 줄이기
rows.en: Shrink your plan until it feels doable

rows.ko: 이번 주 공부나 준비 계획 하나를 적고, 정말 해낼 수 있을지 마음속으로 가늠해 보세요. 자신이 없으면 시간이나 분량을 줄여 다시 쓰고, 못 한 날은 게으름이 아니라 크기를 고치라는 신호로 봅니다.
rows.en: Write down one study or prep plan for this week, and ask yourself honestly whether you can pull it off. If you're unsure, rewrite it with less time or a smaller goal. On days it doesn't happen, don't call it laziness. Read it as a sign the plan needs resizing.
rows.en_before_tone: Try writing down one study or prep plan for this week and quietly gauging whether you can really do it. If you're not confident, rewrite it with less time or a smaller amount, and treat days you don't manage it not as laziness but as a sign to adjust the size.

rows.ko: 계획이 너무 크면 못 한 날 자책만 남기 쉽습니다. 해낼 만한 크기로 줄여 지켜 내는 경험이 쌓이면 나에 대한 믿음도 단단해져요.
rows.en: An oversized plan turns every missed day into self-blame. Keep your plans to a size you can honor, and your trust in yourself grows steadfast.
rows.en_before_tone: When a plan is too big, missed days tend to leave only self-blame. As you keep plans that are sized to fit, your trust in yourself grows steadier.

rows.ko: 보이는 것, 만져지는 것 순으로 주의를 지금 여기로 돌리기
rows.en: Ground yourself in the present: first what you see, then what you touch
rows.en_before_tone: Bring your attention to the here and now: first what you see, then what you touch

rows.ko: 공부를 시작하기 전이나 불안이 올라올 때, 눈에 보이는 것 몇 가지와 손에 닿는 것 몇 가지를 차례로 속으로 짚어 보세요. 발바닥이 바닥에 닿는 느낌으로 마무리해도 좋습니다.
rows.en: Before you start studying, or whenever anxiety rises, silently name a few things you can see, then a few things you can touch. Finish by feeling your feet on the floor.
rows.en_before_tone: Before you start studying or when anxiety rises, try silently naming a few things you can see, then a few things you can touch. You can finish with the feeling of your feet on the floor.

rows.ko: 앞날 걱정에 머리가 바쁠 때 감각은 마음을 지금 여기로 데려와요. 지금 할 수 있는 일로 돌아오기도 한결 쉬워집니다.
rows.en: When your head races ahead with worry, your senses bring you back to the here and now. From there, you return easily to what you can do right now.
rows.en_before_tone: When your head is busy worrying about the future, your senses bring your mind back to the here and now. It also becomes much easier to return to what you can do right now.

rows.ko: 알아가는 사람이 반응해준 순간과 조마조마했던 순간 적기
rows.en: Note when the person you're getting to know responded, and when you felt on edge
rows.en_before_tone: Write down moments the person you're getting to know responded, and moments you felt on edge

rows.ko: 요즘 알아가거나 만나는 사람이 있다면 최근을 떠올려, 내 연락이나 이야기에 반응해 줬던 순간과 조마조마했던 순간을 한 줄씩 적어 보세요. 관계를 판정하는 시험이 아니라 나에게 편안한 관계의 모습을 알아보는 연습입니다.
rows.en: If you're getting to know or seeing someone, look back over recent days and write one line each: a moment they responded to your message or story, and a moment you felt on edge. This isn't a test of the relationship. It's practice in noticing what feels comfortable to you.
rows.en_before_tone: If there's someone you're getting to know or seeing, try thinking back over recent days and writing one line each: a moment they responded to your message or story, and a moment you felt on edge. It's not a test to judge the relationship; it's practice in noticing what a comfortable relationship looks like for you.

rows.ko: 안정감은 설렘의 크기보다 꾸준히 반응해 주는 순간에서 자라요. 반응해 준 순간을 눈으로 확인하면 불안한 해석에 덜 휩쓸립니다.
rows.en: Security grows from steady moments of being answered, more than from how strong the butterflies are. Seeing those moments with your own eyes keeps anxious guesses from sweeping you away.
rows.en_before_tone: A sense of security grows from steady moments of responsiveness more than from how strong the butterflies are. Seeing those moments with your own eyes makes you less likely to get swept up in anxious interpretations.

rows.ko: 다음 주의 가장 바쁜 날 알려주기
rows.en: Tell each other your busiest day next week
rows.en_before_tone: Share your busiest day next week

rows.ko: 서로 바쁠 것 같은 날을 미리 알려 주고, 그날은 연락이 뜸해도 괜찮은지 기대를 맞춰 보세요. 짧은 대화로도 충분합니다.
rows.en: Give each other a heads-up about which days look busy, and agree on whether lighter texting is okay on those days. A quick chat is all it takes.
rows.en_before_tone: Try letting each other know ahead of time which days are likely to be busy, and agreeing on whether it's okay to be in touch less on those days. A short conversation is enough.

rows.ko: 연락이 줄어든 이유를 모르면 마음이 나쁜 쪽으로 해석하기 쉽습니다. 미리 알면 기다리는 시간이 훨씬 편안해져요.
rows.en: When messages slow down and you don't know why, your mind races to the worst. A heads-up turns the wait into something easy.
rows.en_before_tone: When you don't know why messages have dropped off, it's easy for your mind to assume the worst. Knowing ahead of time makes the waiting much more comfortable.

rows.ko: 연인이 있을 때
rows.en: If you're in a relationship

rows.ko: 마음이 놓이는 장소 하나를 감각으로 채워두기
rows.en: Fill a calming place with all your senses
rows.en_before_tone: Fill one calming place with your senses

rows.ko: 편안했던 장소나 순간 하나를 정해 보이는 것·소리·냄새·촉감을 한 줄씩 적어 보세요. 답장을 기다리며 마음이 불안할 때 잠깐 떠올릴 수 있게 짧게 줄여 둡니다.
rows.en: Choose one place or moment where you felt truly at ease, and write one line each for what you saw, heard, smelled, and felt. Keep it short, so you can call it up in a heartbeat when waiting for a reply makes you anxious.
rows.en_before_tone: Try choosing one place or moment where you felt at ease, and writing one line each for what you saw, heard, smelled, and felt. Keep it short so you can bring it to mind quickly when you feel anxious waiting for a reply.

rows.ko: 마음이 쉴 수 있는 곳을 정해 두면 불안이 올라올 때 돌아갈 자리가 생깁니다. 상대의 반응과 상관없이 스스로 마음을 놓는 연습이에요.
rows.en: A go-to place where your mind can rest gives you somewhere to return when anxiety rises. This is how you practice calming yourself, whatever the other person does.
rows.en_before_tone: Having a set place where your mind can rest gives you somewhere to return when anxiety rises. It's practice in settling yourself, regardless of how the other person responds.

rows.ko: 바꿀 수 없는 조건 옆에 '그래도 할 수 있는 일' 적기
rows.en: Next to what you can't change, write 'what I can still do'

rows.ko: 가족 일 중 지금 당장 바꿀 수 없는 조건 하나를 적고, 그 옆에 그래도 내가 할 수 있는 일 하나를 적어 보세요. 바꿀 수 있는 것까지 포기하자는 뜻은 아닙니다.
rows.en: Write down one family situation you can't change right now, and beside it, one thing you can still do. This isn't about giving up on what you can change.
rows.en_before_tone: Try writing down one family circumstance you can't change right now, and next to it, one thing you can still do. This doesn't mean giving up on what you can change.

rows.ko: 가족 걱정은 내 힘 밖의 일까지 끌어안기 쉬워요. 할 수 있는 한 가지에 힘을 모으면 나머지는 조금 내려놓을 수 있습니다.
rows.en: Family worries pull in things far beyond your control. Pour your energy into the one thing you can do, and you loosen your grip on the rest.
rows.en_before_tone: Family worries easily pull in things beyond your control. When you focus your energy on the one thing you can do, you can set the rest down a little.

rows.ko: 즉흥이 아닌 정해진 만남으로 관계를 이어가기
rows.en: Stay in touch on a schedule, not on a whim
rows.en_before_tone: Keep the relationship going with set times, not spur-of-the-moment ones

rows.ko: 가족과의 통화나 만남을 그때그때 정하기보다 '주말 저녁 통화'처럼 정해 둔 날로 이어 가 보세요. 길지 않아도 꾸준한 것이 중요합니다.
rows.en: Instead of calling or visiting family whenever it happens to come up, set regular times, like 'a call on weekend evenings.' It doesn't have to be long. Consistency is what counts.
rows.en_before_tone: Rather than arranging calls or visits with family as they come up, try keeping them going on set days, like 'a weekend evening call.' It doesn't need to be long; being steady is what matters.

rows.ko: 언제 연락이 닿을지 알면 사이사이 걱정이 줄어듭니다. 예측할 수 있는 연결은 그 자체로 안정감을 줘요.
rows.en: Knowing when you'll next connect takes the edge off the worry in between. A predictable rhythm of contact is its own source of security.
rows.en_before_tone: Knowing when you'll be in touch eases the worry in between. A predictable connection brings a sense of stability in itself.

rows.ko: 내 방에서 가장 아늑한 자리 찾기
rows.en: Find the coziest spot in your room

rows.ko: 집 안에서 가장 편안한 자리를 찾아 담요나 쿠션 같은 작은 물건 하나로 더 아늑하게 꾸며 보세요. 마음이 복잡한 날 그 자리에 잠깐 앉아 있기만 하면 됩니다.
rows.en: Find the most comfortable spot at home and make it cozier with one small touch, like a blanket or a cushion. On days your head feels tangled, simply go and sit there for a while.
rows.en_before_tone: Try finding the most comfortable spot at home and making it cozier with one small item, like a blanket or cushion. On days your mind feels tangled, you can just sit there for a little while.

rows.ko: 몸이 편히 머무는 자리가 있으면 마음도 기댈 곳이 생겨요. 가족 일로 흔들릴 때 돌아올 나만의 쉼터가 됩니다.
rows.en: When your body has a place to truly unwind, your mind finds something to lean on too. That spot becomes your sanctum (private refuge) whenever family matters shake you.
rows.en_before_tone: When your body has a place to rest easy, your mind gets something to lean on too. It becomes your own shelter to come back to when family matters shake you.

rows.ko: 확신하기 전에 다른 가능성을 생각해보기
rows.en: Before you decide it's true, consider other explanations
rows.en_before_tone: Before you're sure, consider other possibilities

rows.ko: 모임 뒤 '나를 싫어하나?' 같은 생각이 들면, 확신하기 전에 그 장면을 설명할 다른 가능성 두 가지를 떠올려 보세요. 피곤했을 수도, 다른 일에 정신이 팔렸을 수도 있습니다.
rows.en: If a thought like 'Do they dislike me?' pops up after a get-together, come up with two other explanations for that moment before you settle on it. They were tired, or their mind was on something else.
rows.en_before_tone: If a thought like 'do they dislike me?' comes up after a get-together, before deciding it's true, try thinking of two other ways to explain that moment. They may have been tired, or distracted by something else.

rows.ko: 불안할 때 마음은 가장 나쁜 해석을 먼저 붙잡기 쉬워요. 다른 가능성을 열어 두기만 해도 관계를 믿을 여지가 생깁니다.
rows.en: Anxiety grabs the worst explanation first. Simply leaving room for other possibilities opens space to trust the friendship.
rows.en_before_tone: When you're anxious, your mind tends to grab the worst interpretation first. Simply keeping other possibilities open makes room to trust the relationship.

rows.ko: 새로운 모임에 가기 전 귀가 계획 세우기
rows.en: Plan your way home before a new get-together
rows.en_before_tone: Plan your way home before a new gathering

rows.ko: 처음 가는 모임이나 행사라면 집에 돌아갈 방법과 나올 시간을 미리 정해 보세요. 정한 시간보다 일찍 나와도 괜찮습니다.
rows.en: If it's a gathering or event you've never been to, decide ahead of time how you'll get home and when you'll head out. Leaving earlier than planned is perfectly fine.
rows.en_before_tone: If it's a gathering or event you've never been to, try deciding in advance how you'll get home and when you'll leave. It's fine to leave earlier than planned.

rows.ko: 끝이 보이면 낯선 자리도 덜 막막합니다. 스스로 정한 안전한 틀이 있으면 그 안에서 마음을 놓기 쉬워요.
rows.en: When you can see the finish line, a new setting feels far less overwhelming. Inside a safety net you've built yourself, you relax and enjoy it.
rows.en_before_tone: When you can see the end, an unfamiliar setting feels less daunting. With a safe frame you've set yourself, it's easier to relax within it.

rows.ko: 모임 후 좋았던 대화 한 가지 기억하기
rows.en: Remember one great conversation after seeing people
rows.en_before_tone: Remember one good conversation after a get-together

rows.ko: 사람들을 만난 뒤 특히 기분 좋았던 대화 주제 하나를 메모해 두세요. 아쉬운 장면보다 이것을 먼저 적는 것이 순서입니다.
rows.en: After seeing people, note one conversation topic that felt especially good. Write it down first, before any moment you wish had gone differently.
rows.en_before_tone: After seeing people, try jotting down one conversation topic that felt especially good. It helps to write this first, before any moments you wish had gone differently.

rows.ko: 모임이 끝나면 아쉬웠던 장면만 오래 남기 쉬워요. 좋았던 순간을 기록해 두면 사람들 사이에서 편안했던 기억도 함께 쌓입니다.
rows.en: After a get-together, the awkward moments tend to linger longest. Record the good ones, and you build a store of memories of feeling at ease around people.
rows.en_before_tone: After a get-together, it's easy for only the awkward moments to linger. Writing down the good moments helps you build up memories of feeling at ease around people, too.

rows.ko: 머릿속 고민을 다 꺼낸 뒤 가장 큰 두 가지만 고르기
rows.en: Pour out every worry, then pick just the top two
rows.en_before_tone: Empty out all your worries, then pick just the two biggest

rows.ko: 돈과 생활에 관해 마음을 무겁게 하는 일을 생각나는 대로 모두 적고, 비슷한 것끼리 묶어 가장 중요한 두 가지만 골라 보세요. 나머지는 '나중에 볼 목록'으로 옮겨 두면 됩니다.
rows.en: Write down everything about money and daily life that weighs on you, in whatever order it comes. Group similar items, then choose the two that matter most. Move the rest to a 'deal with later' list.
rows.en_before_tone: Try writing down everything about money and daily life that's weighing on you, as it comes to mind, grouping similar ones together, and picking just the two most important. The rest can go on a 'look at later' list.

rows.ko: 걱정이 한꺼번에 몰리면 모든 게 다 급해 보입니다. 큰 두 가지만 남기면 나머지는 잠시 내려놓을 수 있어요.
rows.en: When worries arrive all at once, everything feels urgent. Keep only the top two in hand, and you set the rest aside for now.
rows.en_before_tone: When worries pile up all at once, everything seems urgent. Keeping just the two biggest lets you set the rest aside for now.

rows.ko: 걱정이 끼어들 때 하던 일의 한 지점으로 눈 돌리기
rows.en: When worry butts in, return your eyes to one spot in your task
rows.en_before_tone: When worry cuts in, bring your eyes back to one spot in what you were doing

rows.ko: 일하거나 쉬는 중에 돈 걱정이 올라와 잔고를 확인하고 싶어지면, 속으로 '걱정이 지나가는 중이네'라고 말해 보세요. 걱정은 그대로 둔 채 하던 일의 구체적인 한 곳으로 눈을 옮깁니다.
rows.en: If money worries surface while you're working or relaxing and you feel the urge to check your balance, tell yourself, 'Just a worry passing through.' Let the worry be, and rest your eyes on one specific spot in whatever you were doing.
rows.en_before_tone: If money worries rise up while you're working or resting and you feel the urge to check your balance, try saying to yourself, 'a worry is passing through.' Leave the worry as it is, and move your eyes to one specific spot in what you were doing.

rows.ko: 걱정과 싸우지 않아도 하던 일은 이어 갈 수 있어요. 확인을 조금 미뤄 보는 경험이 쌓이면 마음이 쫓기는 느낌도 줄어듭니다.
rows.en: You can carry on with what you were doing without battling the worry. Each time you delay that check a little, the feeling of being chased fades.
rows.en_before_tone: You can keep doing what you were doing without fighting the worry. As you get used to putting off checking for a little while, the feeling of being chased eases.

rows.ko: 매일 비슷한 시간에 자고 일어나는 리듬을 만들기
rows.en: Build a rhythm of sleeping and waking at the same time
rows.en_before_tone: Build a rhythm of sleeping and waking at similar times each day

rows.ko: 이번 주에는 잠드는 시간과 일어나는 시간을 비슷하게 맞춰 보세요. 주말에도 크게 벗어나지 않는 것이 핵심입니다.
rows.en: This week, keep your bedtime and wake-up time about the same each day. The key is not drifting far from them on weekends, either.
rows.en_before_tone: This week, try keeping your bedtime and wake-up time about the same. The key is not straying far from it on weekends either.

rows.ko: 돈 문제처럼 당장 바꾸기 어려운 걱정이 있을 때, 하루의 리듬은 내가 지킬 수 있는 안정의 바탕이 됩니다. 몸이 안정되면 생각도 덜 흔들려요.
rows.en: Money worries rarely resolve overnight, but your daily rhythm is a source of stability you truly own. Steady your body, and your mind steadies with it.
rows.en_before_tone: When you have worries that are hard to change right away, like money matters, the rhythm of your day becomes a base of stability you can protect. When your body feels steady, your thoughts sway less too.

rows.ko: 내가 도와줄 수 있는 범위 구체화하기
rows.en: Define how much help you can offer
rows.en_before_tone: Spell out how much you can help

rows.ko: 새로운 요청을 받으면 바로 '네'라고 하기 전에 지금 가능한 부분과 어려운 부분을 나눠 보세요. '이 부분은 이번 주에 가능하고, 나머지는 다음 주가 될 것 같아요'처럼 말해 봅니다.
rows.en: Before you say 'yes' to a new request, separate what you can do now from what's a stretch. Then say it plainly: 'I can finish this part this week, and the rest by next week.'
rows.en_before_tone: When you get a new request, before saying 'yes' right away, try separating what you can do now from what's hard. You might say something like, 'I can do this part this week, and the rest will probably be next week.'

rows.ko: 다 받거나 다 거절하는 것 말고도 선택지가 있어요. 범위를 분명히 하면 동료도 계획을 세우기 쉬워집니다.
rows.en: You have more choices than all or nothing. Spell out what you can take on, and your coworkers can plan around it with ease.
rows.en_before_tone: There are options besides accepting everything or refusing everything. Making the scope clear also makes it easier for coworkers to plan.

rows.ko: 재직 중일 때
rows.en: If you're currently working

rows.ko: 회의 없는 짧은 시간 직접 확보하기
rows.en: Carve out a short, meeting-free block for yourself
rows.en_before_tone: Block out a short meeting-free time yourself

rows.ko: 일정표에 짧은 집중 시간을 하나 막아 두고, 그동안에는 한 가지 작업만 해 보세요. 일정 이름을 '집중 시간'으로 적어 두면 지키기가 더 쉽습니다.
rows.en: Block off one short stretch of focus time on your calendar and give it to a single task. Name it 'Focus time' so you honor it.
rows.en_before_tone: Try blocking out one short focus slot in your calendar and working on just one task during it. Naming the slot 'Focus time' makes it easier to protect.

rows.ko: 내 시간을 지키는 일도 경계를 세우는 연습입니다. 비워 둔 시간이 있으면 쏟아지는 요청 속에서도 숨 쉴 틈이 생겨요.
rows.en: Guarding your time is boundary work too. Clear space on your calendar lets you breathe, even when requests pour in.
rows.en_before_tone: Protecting your time is also practice in setting boundaries. Having some time kept clear gives you room to breathe even amid a flood of requests.

rows.ko: 재직 중일 때
rows.en: If you're currently working

rows.ko: 퇴근을 알리는 마지막 파일 닫기
rows.en: Make closing your last file your end-of-day ritual
rows.tone_reason: 2026-11-05 신비 톤 수정분 v2.2: 섹션 제목은 유지하고, 제안 안에서 'small ritual'로
rows.en_before_tone: Close the last file to mark the end of your workday

rows.ko: 업무를 마칠 때 작업 파일을 정리하고 내일 첫 행동만 남겨 둔 뒤 창을 모두 닫아 보세요. 이 동작을 퇴근 신호로 삼습니다.
rows.en: As you wrap up work, tidy your files, jot down tomorrow's first step, and close every window. Let that be your signal that the workday is over.
rows.en_before_tone: When you finish work, try tidying your work files, leaving just tomorrow's first step, and closing all your windows. Let this action be your signal that the workday is over.

rows.ko: 일과 쉼 사이에 분명한 선이 있으면 퇴근 뒤에도 일이 덜 따라옵니다. 하루의 끝을 내가 정하는 작은 연습이에요.
rows.en: Draw a clear line between work and rest, and far less work follows you home. You decide when your day ends.
rows.en_before_tone: With a clear line between work and rest, work follows you home less. It's a small practice in deciding when your day ends.

rows.ko: 재직 중일 때
rows.en: If you're currently working

rows.ko: 붙들고 있는 목표에 '누가 정한 기준?' 묻고 내 말로 다시 쓰기
rows.en: Ask 'Whose standard is this?' about a goal you're clinging to, then rewrite it in your own words
rows.en_before_tone: Ask 'whose standard is this?' about a goal you're holding on to, and rewrite it in your own words

rows.ko: 요즘 마음을 쓰는 진로 목표 하나를 적고, 그 기준이 어디서 왔는지 부모님·회사·SNS·나 중에서 표시해 보세요. 그다음 '내가 원하는 삶에서는 이 정도면 충분하다'처럼 내 말로 한 번 다시 써 봅니다.
rows.en: Write down one career goal on your mind and mark where its standard came from: your parents, your workplace, social media, or you. Then rewrite it in your own words, something like 'For the life I want, this is enough.'
rows.en_before_tone: Try writing down one career goal you've been focused on lately, and marking where that standard came from: parents, work, social media, or you. Then rewrite it once in your own words, like 'for the life I want, this much is enough.'

rows.ko: 어떤 삶이 좋은지는 내가 정할 수 있어요. 기준의 주인을 확인하는 것만으로도 남의 기대와 내 기준 사이에 선이 생깁니다.
rows.en: You get to define what a good life looks like. Simply asking whose standard you're following draws a line between other people's expectations and your own.
rows.en_before_tone: You get to decide what a good life is. Just checking whose standard it is draws a line between others' expectations and your own.

rows.ko: 잠깐이라도 방해받지 않는 시간을 확보하기
rows.en: Claim uninterrupted time, even a sliver
rows.en_before_tone: Secure time without interruptions, even briefly

rows.ko: 공부나 자기계발을 하는 동안 휴대폰을 멀리 두고, 함께 사는 사람에게 '이 시간만은 방해하지 말아 줘'라고 알려 보세요. 짧아도 온전히 지켜지는 시간이 중요합니다.
rows.en: When you sit down to study or grow, put your phone out of reach and tell the people you live with: 'Please don't interrupt me for a bit.' Even a short stretch counts when it's truly yours.
rows.en_before_tone: While you study or work on self-improvement, try putting your phone away and telling the people you live with, 'Please don't interrupt me during this time.' Even if it's short, time that's fully protected is what matters.

rows.ko: 내 시간을 지켜 달라고 말하는 것도 선을 긋는 일입니다. 방해받지 않는 시간이 쌓이면 나와의 약속을 믿을 수 있어요.
rows.en: Asking others to respect your time is boundary-setting too. Every uninterrupted hour you claim builds trust in the promises you make to yourself.
rows.en_before_tone: Asking others to respect your time is also a way of drawing a line. As uninterrupted time builds up, you can trust the promises you make to yourself.

rows.ko: 타인과 나를 비교하는 습관을 의식적으로 줄이기
rows.en: Consciously step back from comparison
rows.en_before_tone: Consciously cut back on comparing yourself to others

rows.ko: 남의 성과가 자주 보이는 앱이나 계정을 하나 골라 쉬는 날을 정해 보세요. 비교가 시작되면 '지금 비교하고 있네' 하고 알아차리는 것까지가 연습입니다.
rows.en: Pick one app or account where other people's wins are always in your face, and schedule days off from it. When comparison kicks in, simply notice 'I'm comparing again.' That noticing is the whole practice.
rows.en_before_tone: Try picking one app or account where you often see others' achievements and setting days to take a break from it. When comparing starts, the practice is simply to notice, 'I'm comparing right now.'

rows.ko: 비교는 남의 속도를 내 기준으로 끌어오기 쉬워요. 들어오는 정보에 선을 그으면 내 속도를 지키기가 한결 수월해집니다.
rows.en: Comparison quietly turns other people's pace into your yardstick. Limit what you take in, and you protect your own rhythm.
rows.en_before_tone: Comparison tends to turn other people's pace into your standard. Drawing a line around the information coming in makes it much easier to keep your own pace.

rows.ko: 연락 빈도에 대한 내 선호 적어두기
rows.en: Write down how often you like to stay in touch
rows.en_before_tone: Write down your preferences for how often to be in touch

rows.ko: 연인이나 알아가는 사람과 연락할 때 편한 주기와 부담스러운 상황을 적어 보세요. 필요할 때 꺼낼 수 있게 다정하게 설명할 문장도 하나 만들어 둡니다.
rows.en: Jot down how often you like to text or talk with a partner or someone new, and which situations start to feel like too much. Keep one kind, simple sentence ready to explain it when the moment comes.
rows.en_before_tone: Try writing down how often you're comfortable being in touch with a partner or someone you're getting to know, and which situations feel like too much. It also helps to prepare one sentence to explain it kindly, so you can use it when needed.

rows.ko: 내 리듬을 먼저 알아야 상대에게도 부드럽게 전할 수 있어요. 문장이 준비돼 있으면 서운함이 쌓이기 전에 말을 꺼내기 쉽습니다.
rows.en: Know your own rhythm first, and you can share it with grace. With your words ready, you speak up before hurt feelings pile up.
rows.en_before_tone: Knowing your own rhythm first lets you share it gently with the other person. With a sentence ready, it's easier to speak up before hurt feelings pile up.

rows.ko: 이번 달 각자 지키고 싶은 개인 일정 공유하기
rows.en: Share the personal time you each want to protect this month
rows.en_before_tone: Share the personal plans you each want to protect this month

rows.ko: 함께하는 일정 말고 각자 중요하게 여기는 시간을 하나씩 알려 주세요. 운동, 친구 모임, 혼자 쉬는 저녁처럼 무엇이든 괜찮습니다.
rows.en: Beyond the plans you make together, tell each other about one block of time that matters to you alone: a workout, a night out with friends, an evening to yourself. Anything counts.
rows.en_before_tone: Besides your plans together, try telling each other one block of time you each consider important. Anything works, like exercise, meeting friends, or an evening resting alone.

rows.ko: 각자의 시간을 미리 알면 서로 서운해할 일이 줄어듭니다. 가까운 사이에서도 나를 지키는 선은 관계를 오래 편안하게 해 줘요.
rows.en: Knowing each other's plans in advance means fewer hurt feelings. Even in a close bond, boundaries that protect you keep love comfortable for the long haul.
rows.en_before_tone: Knowing each other's time in advance means fewer hurt feelings. Even in a close relationship, boundaries that protect you keep the relationship comfortable for longer.

rows.ko: 연인이 있을 때
rows.en: If you're in a relationship

rows.ko: 관계와 별개로 나를 채우는 활동을 이어가기
rows.en: Keep doing what recharges you outside the relationship
rows.en_before_tone: Keep up activities that fill you up, apart from the relationship

rows.ko: 연애와 상관없이 나를 즐겁게 하는 활동 하나를 정해 이번 주에도 이어 가 보세요. 혼자 하는 취미든 친구와의 약속이든 좋습니다.
rows.en: Choose one activity that delights you, love life aside, and keep it going this week. A solo hobby or plans with friends both count.
rows.en_before_tone: Try choosing one activity that makes you happy regardless of your love life, and keeping it going this week too. A solo hobby or plans with friends both work.

rows.ko: 관계 밖에도 나를 채우는 곳이 있으면 상대에게 모든 걸 기대지 않아도 됩니다. 그 여유가 건강한 선을 지키는 힘이 돼요.
rows.en: When other parts of your life fill you up, you don't need your partner to be everything. That breathing room is your strength for holding healthy boundaries.
rows.en_before_tone: When you have places outside the relationship that fill you up, you don't have to depend on the other person for everything. That breathing room becomes the strength to keep healthy boundaries.

rows.ko: 챙기는 사람·일을 '고른 것 / 떠맡은 것'으로 나누고 하나 덜어보기
rows.en: Sort the people and tasks you look after into 'chosen / taken on,' and lighten one
rows.en_before_tone: Sort the people and tasks you look after into 'chosen / taken on' and lighten one

rows.ko: 요즘 가족 안에서 챙기고 있는 사람과 일을 한 장에 적고, '내가 고른 것'과 '떠맡은 것' 중 가까운 쪽을 표시해 보세요. 떠맡은 것 중 하나는 이번 주에 나누거나 줄여 봅니다.
rows.en: On a single page, list the people and tasks you've been tending to in your family lately, and mark whether each feels more like 'something I chose' or 'something I took on.' This week, share or scale back one thing you took on.
rows.en_before_tone: On one page, try writing the people and tasks you've been looking after in your family lately, and marking whether each is closer to 'something I chose' or 'something I took on.' This week, you might share or reduce one of the things you took on.

rows.ko: 챙기는 일에는 내가 아끼는 마음이 담겨 있어요. 고른 것은 지키고 떠맡은 것은 덜어 내야 오래 다정할 수 있습니다.
rows.en: Caring for family comes from love. Protect what you chose, lighten what you took on, and your kindness lasts for the long run.
rows.en_before_tone: Looking after others carries your care for them. Keeping what you chose and lightening what you took on is how you can stay kind for the long run.

rows.ko: 불편한 농담에 내 마음 짧게 표현하기
rows.en: Say in a few words how an uncomfortable joke landed
rows.en_before_tone: Briefly express how you feel about an uncomfortable joke

rows.ko: 가족 모임에서 불편한 농담이나 질문을 들으면, 안전한 분위기에서 '그 얘기는 좀 불편해요'처럼 짧게 알려 보세요. 미리 문장 하나를 정해 두면 꺼내기 쉽습니다.
rows.en: When someone at a family gathering makes a joke or asks a question that makes you uncomfortable, and it feels safe, say so briefly: 'I'm not really comfortable with that topic.' Keep the line ready in advance so it comes easily.
rows.en_before_tone: If you hear an uncomfortable joke or question at a family gathering, and it feels safe to do so, try letting them know briefly, like 'I'm a bit uncomfortable with that topic.' Deciding on a sentence in advance makes it easier to say.

rows.ko: 가족이라도 듣기 힘든 말에는 선을 그을 수 있어요. 짧고 차분하게 말하면 관계를 해치지 않으면서 나를 지킬 수 있습니다.
rows.en: Family or not, you have every right to draw a line at hurtful comments. Keep it short and calm, and you stand up for yourself without harming the relationship.
rows.en_before_tone: Even with family, you can draw a line at words that are hard to hear. Speaking briefly and calmly lets you protect yourself without harming the relationship.

rows.ko: 집 앞을 잠깐 걸으며 기분 전환하기
rows.en: Take a quick walk around the block to reset
rows.en_before_tone: Take a short walk outside to reset

rows.ko: 가족과 함께 있는 시간이 길어져 마음이 답답해지면, 잠깐 바람 쐬고 오겠다고 말하고 집 앞을 걸어 보세요. 돌아오는 시간도 미리 정해 두면 마음이 편합니다.
rows.en: When a long stretch with family starts to feel stifling, say you're stepping out for fresh air and walk around the block. Decide ahead of time when you'll be back, and you'll relax more easily.
rows.en_before_tone: When long stretches with family start to feel stifling, try saying you're stepping out for some fresh air and taking a walk outside your home. Deciding ahead of time when you'll be back makes it easier.

rows.ko: 잠시 떨어져 있는 것도 관계를 지키는 방법이에요. 걷는 동안 몸이 풀리면 다시 돌아가 대화할 여유가 생깁니다.
rows.en: Stepping away for a moment protects the relationship too. As you walk, your body loosens, and you return with room to talk.
rows.en_before_tone: Stepping away for a while is also a way to protect a relationship. As your body loosens while you walk, you'll have more room to go back and talk.

rows.ko: 최근 거절해서 잘했다고 느낀 일 떠올리기
rows.en: Recall a recent 'no' you're glad you said
rows.en_before_tone: Recall a recent time you were glad you said no

rows.ko: 친구나 모임 요청을 거절해서 잘했다고 느낀 선택 하나를 떠올려, 그 덕분에 무엇을 지켰는지 적어 보세요. 쉼, 일정, 컨디션처럼 작은 것이어도 충분합니다.
rows.en: Think of one time you turned down a friend or a group invite and felt good about it, then write down what that 'no' protected. Something small, like rest, your schedule, or your energy, is plenty.
rows.en_before_tone: Try thinking of one time you turned down a friend's or group's request and felt good about it, and writing down what you protected by doing so. Something small, like rest, your schedule, or your energy, is enough.

rows.ko: 거절 뒤에는 미안함이 더 오래 남기 쉬워요. 거절로 지킨 것을 확인해 두면 다음 거절이 조금 덜 무겁습니다.
rows.en: Guilt tends to linger after you say no. Name what you protected, and the next no feels lighter.
rows.en_before_tone: After saying no, guilt tends to linger longer. Noting what you protected makes the next no a little less heavy.

rows.ko: 모임 불참 메시지 짧게 준비하기
rows.en: Keep a short 'can't make it' message ready
rows.en_before_tone: Prepare a short message for skipping a get-together

rows.ko: 쉬고 싶은 날 쓸 수 있는 정중한 불참 문장을 미리 하나 써서 메모장에 저장해 두세요. '이번엔 쉬어 갈게, 다음에 꼭 보자'처럼 짧을수록 좋습니다.
rows.en: Write one polite message in advance for days you'd rather rest, and save it in your notes app. Short is best: 'I'm going to sit this one out, but I'd love to catch up next time!'
rows.en_before_tone: Try writing one polite message ahead of time for days you want to rest, and saving it in your notes. The shorter the better, like 'I'll sit this one out, but let's definitely meet next time.'

rows.ko: 그 자리에서 거절할 말을 찾으려면 마음이 급해집니다. 준비된 문장이 있으면 미안함에 끌려가지 않고 내 선택을 지킬 수 있어요.
rows.en: Scrambling for a no on the spot puts you under pressure. With a message ready, you hold to your decision instead of getting swept along by guilt.
rows.en_before_tone: Trying to find words to say no on the spot makes you feel rushed. With a sentence ready, you can stand by your choice without being pulled along by guilt.

rows.ko: 사람을 만나지 않는 저녁을 의도적으로 만들기
rows.en: Make one people-free evening your small ritual
rows.tone_reason: 2026-11-05 신비 톤 수정분 v2.2: 섹션 제목은 유지하고, 제안 안에서 'small ritual'로
rows.en_before_tone: Intentionally set aside an evening without seeing people

rows.ko: 이번 주 저녁 하루를 골라 약속을 잡지 않는 날로 비워 두세요. 그날은 연락에도 바로 답하지 않아도 됩니다.
rows.en: Pick one evening this week and leave it free of plans. That night, messages can wait.
rows.en_before_tone: Try choosing one evening this week and keeping it free of plans. That day, you don't have to reply to messages right away either.

rows.ko: 사람을 좋아해도 혼자 회복하는 시간은 필요해요. 비워 둔 저녁이 있어야 다른 날의 만남도 더 즐겁게 누릴 수 있습니다.
rows.en: Even if you love people, you need time alone to recharge. One free evening lets you savor time with friends on the other days.
rows.en_before_tone: Even if you love people, you need time to recharge alone. Having an evening set aside lets you enjoy time with others more on other days.

rows.ko: 내가 지키고 싶은 일상의 규칙 한 줄 쓰기
rows.en: Write down one everyday rule you want to keep
rows.en_before_tone: Write one line about an everyday rule you want to keep

rows.ko: 돈과 관련해 나를 위해 지키고 싶은 작은 원칙 하나를 문장으로 적어 보세요. '돈을 빌려줄 때는 하루 생각하고 답한다'처럼 구체적일수록 좋습니다.
rows.en: Put one small money rule you want to keep for yourself into a single sentence. The more specific the better: 'If someone asks to borrow money, I'll sleep on it before I answer.'
rows.en_before_tone: Try writing down, as a sentence, one small money-related principle you want to keep for yourself. The more specific the better, like 'When lending money, I'll take a day to think before answering.'

rows.ko: 기준이 미리 있으면 부탁을 받거나 사고 싶은 게 생길 때 흔들림이 줄어요. 정해 둔 한 줄이 나 대신 선을 그어 줍니다.
rows.en: Set a rule in advance, and you waver less when someone asks for a favor or something catches your eye. That one line holds the boundary for you.
rows.en_before_tone: When you've set a rule ahead of time, you waver less when someone asks for a favor or something catches your eye. That one line you decided on draws the boundary for you.

rows.ko: 충동 행동에 장단점 네 칸 채우기
rows.en: Fill in a four-box pros and cons list for an impulse
rows.en_before_tone: Fill in four pros-and-cons boxes for an impulse

rows.ko: 자꾸 하게 되는 충동구매 하나를 골라, 샀을 때와 사지 않고 넘겼을 때의 좋은 점·나쁜 점 네 칸을 채워 휴대폰에 저장해 두세요. 같은 충동이 오면 결제 전에 꺼내 읽어 봅니다.
rows.en: Pick one impulse purchase you keep making and fill in four boxes: the pros and cons of buying it, and the pros and cons of letting it go. Save it on your phone, and when the urge returns, read it before you check out.
rows.en_before_tone: Try picking one impulse buy you keep making and fill in four boxes: the upsides and downsides of buying it, and of letting it pass. Save it on your phone. When the same urge shows up, you can pull it out and read it before you pay.

rows.ko: 당장의 마음과 나중의 내가 바라는 것을 나란히 놓으면 고르기가 쉬워져요. 지출에 선을 긋는 것은 참는 일이 아니라 나를 챙기는 일입니다.
rows.en: Put what you want right now beside what your future self wants, and the choice gets clearer. Setting limits on spending isn't denying yourself. It's taking care of yourself.
rows.en_before_tone: Putting what you want right now next to what your future self wants makes the choice easier. Drawing a line on spending isn't about holding back. It's about taking care of yourself.

rows.ko: 부담 없는 선에서 나를 기쁘게 하는 것들을 정해두기
rows.en: List easy, low-cost things that make you happy
rows.en_before_tone: Choose a few low-cost things that make you happy

rows.ko: 돈이 거의 들지 않으면서 나를 기쁘게 하는 것들을 몇 가지 적어 두세요. 산책, 좋아하는 노래, 도서관 나들이처럼 소박할수록 좋습니다.
rows.en: Write down a few things that cost next to nothing yet still lift your mood. The simpler the better: a walk, a favorite song, an afternoon at the library.
rows.en_before_tone: Try writing down a few things that cost almost nothing but make you happy. The simpler the better: a walk, a favorite song, a trip to the library.

rows.ko: 기분을 돌보는 방법이 소비 하나뿐이면 지출의 선을 지키기 어렵습니다. 부담 없는 즐거움이 있으면 무리한 요청이나 유혹에도 덜 흔들려요.
rows.en: If shopping is your only way to cheer up, spending limits are hard to keep. Stock up on easy, low-cost joys, and pushy requests and temptations lose their pull.
rows.en_before_tone: If spending is your only way to lift your mood, it's hard to keep your spending boundaries. Having easy, low-cost joys helps you stay steady against pushy requests and temptations.

rows.ko: 다음 회의에서 확인할 한 문장 준비하기
rows.en: Prepare one question for your next meeting
rows.en_before_tone: Prepare one sentence to check something in your next meeting

rows.ko: 회의 전에 꼭 확인하거나 말하고 싶은 것 하나를 질문 문장으로 적어 두세요. '이 부분은 제가 이렇게 이해했는데 맞을까요?'처럼 쓰면 꺼내기 쉽습니다.
rows.en: Before a meeting, write down one thing you want to confirm or raise, framed as a question. Something like "Here's how I understood this part. Did I get that right?" slips in easily.
rows.en_before_tone: Before a meeting, try writing down one thing you want to confirm or say, phrased as a question. Something like "Here's how I understood this part. Is that right?" makes it easier to bring up.

rows.ko: 말할 문장이 준비돼 있으면 타이밍을 놓쳐도 다시 꺼낼 수 있어요. 미리 쓴 한 줄이 목소리를 내는 출발점이 됩니다.
rows.en: With your words ready, you can bring it up even after the moment passes. That one line you wrote ahead of time is where your voice begins.
rows.en_before_tone: With a sentence ready, you can still bring it up even if you miss the moment. One line written in advance becomes the starting point for using your voice.

rows.ko: 재직 중일 때
rows.en: If you're currently working

rows.ko: 회의 중 작은 의견부터 말하는 연습을 하기
rows.en: Start small: share one opinion in a meeting
rows.en_before_tone: Practice voicing a small opinion in meetings

rows.ko: 다음 회의에서 '저도 그 방향이 좋아 보여요'처럼 짧은 의견 하나를 소리 내어 말해 보세요. 동의나 질문도 훌륭한 의견입니다.
rows.en: At your next meeting, voice one short opinion out loud, like "I like that direction too." Agreeing or asking a question is a real contribution.
rows.en_before_tone: At your next meeting, try saying one short opinion out loud, like "That direction looks good to me too." Agreeing or asking a question counts as a great contribution.

rows.ko: 작은 말이라도 한 번 해 보면 다음 발언의 문턱이 낮아집니다. 내 목소리가 회의에 있다는 감각이 조금씩 자라요.
rows.en: Say even one small thing, and the next time gets easier. Bit by bit, you feel your voice belongs in the room.
rows.en_before_tone: Saying even one small thing lowers the bar for speaking up next time. Little by little, you'll feel that your voice belongs in the room.

rows.ko: 재직 중일 때
rows.en: If you're currently working

rows.ko: 일이 쌓이기 전에 지금 상황 알리기
rows.en: Give a heads-up before work piles up
rows.en_before_tone: Share where things stand before work piles up

rows.ko: 일정이 빠듯하거나 업무가 몰릴 것 같으면 문제가 커지기 전에 담당자에게 지금 상황을 짧게 알려 보세요. '이 일은 이번 주 안에는 어렵고, 이렇게 하면 가능할 것 같아요'처럼 대안을 붙이면 좋습니다.
rows.en: If deadlines look tight or work is about to pile up, give the person in charge a quick update before it snowballs. Offer an alternative with it: "I can't finish this by Friday, but here's what will work."
rows.en_before_tone: If deadlines look tight or work seems about to pile up, try giving the person in charge a short update before it turns into a bigger problem. It helps to add an alternative, like "This won't be possible this week, but here's how it could work."

rows.ko: 힘든 상황을 늦게 말할수록 말하기도 어렵고 수습할 일도 커집니다. 미리 전하는 것은 핑계가 아니라 함께 일하는 사람을 위한 정보예요.
rows.en: The longer you sit on a tough situation, the harder it is to raise and the bigger the cleanup. Flagging it early isn't making excuses. It's valuable information for the people you work with.
rows.en_before_tone: The longer you wait to mention a tough situation, the harder it is to say and the more there is to fix. Speaking up early isn't making excuses. It's useful information for the people you work with.

rows.ko: 재직 중일 때
rows.en: If you're currently working

rows.ko: 말하기 전에 글로 먼저 정리하며 감정을 선명하게 하기
rows.en: Write it out before you talk it out, and get clear on how you feel
