rows.ko: 그 기준을 지키기 위해 주변에 미리 알려 두고 싶은 말은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: To protect those basics, what would you like to tell the people around you up front?
rows.en_before_tone: To keep those standards, what would you like to let the people around you know ahead of time?

rows.ko: 선 지키기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 남의 일정에 맞추다 보면 잠과 식사 같은 기본 리듬부터 흔들리기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 건강한 생활은 새 습관을 더하는 것만큼, 이미 있는 루틴을 지켜 내는 선에서 시작돼요.
rows.en: For you, boundaries take effort, and fitting into everyone else's schedule throws off the basics first, like sleep and meals. {{기질문장}} Healthy living means adding new habits, yes, but it starts with guarding the routines you already have.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find holding boundaries draining often find that adjusting to others' schedules shakes their basic rhythms first, like sleep and meals. {{기질문장}} A healthy life starts with adding new habits, but also with drawing lines that protect the routines you already have.

rows.ko: 돈과 관련해 어디까지가 나의 몫인가
rows.en: When it comes to money, what's really yours to cover?
rows.en_before_tone: When it comes to money, where does your share end?

rows.ko: 거절하지 못해 쓰게 된 돈을 떠올리면, 그때 어떤 마음이 들었나요?
rows.en: Think of money you spent because you couldn't say no. How did it feel?
rows.en_before_tone: Think of money you spent because you couldn't say no. How did you feel then?

rows.ko: 모임비나 선물처럼 관계 때문에 나가는 지출에 나만의 기준을 세운다면 어떤 모습일까요?
rows.en: If you set your own rules for social spending, like group outings or gifts, what would they be?
rows.en_before_tone: If you set your own standard for relationship-related spending, like group outing costs or gifts, what would it look like?

rows.ko: 마음이 편한 생활을 위해 줄이고 싶은 지출은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: What spending will you cut back on to feel more at ease day to day?
rows.en_before_tone: What spending would you like to cut back on for a life that feels more at ease?

rows.ko: 선 지키기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 관계를 지키려다 내 생활비의 선까지 넘기기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 경제적 여유는 많이 버는 것만큼, 어디까지 쓸지 스스로 정해 두는 기준에서 생겨요.
rows.en: When holding boundaries is hard, protecting relationships pushes you past the limits of your own budget. {{기질문장}} Financial ease comes from earning, and just as much from deciding for yourself how far you're willing to spend. Set that line now.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find holding boundaries draining can end up going past the limits of their own living budget while trying to protect relationships. {{기질문장}} Financial ease comes from earning more, but also from deciding for yourself how much you'll spend.

rows.ko: 인정받기 위해 넘지 않아야 할 선은 어디인가
rows.en: What line won't you cross, even for recognition?
rows.en_before_tone: What line shouldn't you cross for the sake of recognition?

rows.ko: 인정받고 싶어서 무리하게 맡았던 일은 어떤 장면으로 기억되나요?
rows.en: Think of a time you took on too much because you wanted to be recognized. What comes to mind?
rows.en_before_tone: Think of a time you took on too much because you wanted recognition. How do you remember it?

rows.ko: 거절하면서도 존중받는 사람을 떠올리면, 그 사람은 어떻게 말하나요?
rows.en: Picture someone who says no and is still respected. How do they put it?
rows.en_before_tone: Think of someone who says no and is still respected. How do they say it?

rows.ko: 내 능력을 보여 주고 싶은 일과 정중히 사양하고 싶은 일은 각각 무엇인가요?
rows.en: Where do you want to show what you can do, and what would you rather politely decline?
rows.en_before_tone: What's something where you'd like to show what you can do, and something you'd like to politely decline?

rows.ko: 선 지키기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 인정을 바랄수록 무리한 요청까지 받아들이기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 할 수 있는 일과 어려운 일을 분명히 말할 때, 오히려 더 믿을 만한 사람으로 인정받을 수 있어요.
rows.en: If boundaries take effort, the more you want recognition, the more readily you say yes to unreasonable requests. {{기질문장}} Be clear about what you can and can't take on. People come to see you as more dependable, not less.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find holding boundaries draining are more likely to accept unreasonable requests the more they want recognition. {{기질문장}} When you're clear about what you can and can't do, you may actually be seen as more reliable.

rows.ko: 나를 나답게 지켜 주는 선은 무엇인가
rows.en: What line keeps you true to yourself?

rows.ko: 남의 기대에 맞추다가 ‘이건 내가 아닌데’ 싶었던 순간은 어떤 장면이었나요?
rows.en: Recall living up to someone else's expectations and catching yourself thinking, 'This isn't me.'
rows.en_before_tone: What was a moment when you were meeting others' expectations and thought, 'This isn't me'?

rows.ko: 누가 뭐라 해도 양보하고 싶지 않은 나의 가치는 무엇인가요?
rows.en: What value would you refuse to give up, no matter what anyone says?
rows.en_before_tone: What value of yours would you not give up, no matter what anyone says?

rows.ko: 나다운 선을 지켰던 순간을 떠올리면 어떤 감정이 남아 있나요?
rows.en: Recall a time you held a line that felt true to you. What feeling stays with you?
rows.en_before_tone: When you think of a moment you held a line that felt true to you, what feeling stays with you?

rows.ko: 선 지키기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 상대에게 맞추는 사이 내가 원하는 것이 흐려지기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 나다움은 무엇을 받아들이고 무엇을 사양할지 스스로 정하는 순간마다 조금씩 또렷해져요.
rows.en: When limits are hard to set, you lose sight of what you want while you're busy adjusting to others. {{기질문장}} Each time you decide for yourself what to accept and what to turn down, your sense of self comes into sharper focus.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find holding boundaries draining can lose sight of what they want while adjusting to others. {{기질문장}} Being yourself grows a little clearer each time you decide for yourself what to accept and what to decline.

rows.ko: 새로 시작하기 위해 무엇을 내려놓을 것인가
rows.en: What will you let go of to make a fresh start?
rows.en_before_tone: What will you set down to make a new start?

rows.ko: 새로운 일을 하고 싶었지만 맡은 일들에 밀려 시작하지 못했던 장면은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: Think of a time you wanted to start something new, but your existing commitments kept getting in the way.
rows.en_before_tone: What was a time you wanted to start something new but couldn't, because your existing commitments got in the way?

rows.ko: 새 출발을 위해 비워 두고 싶은 시간이나 공간은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: What time or space would you like to keep clear for a fresh start?

rows.ko: 이제는 정중하게 내려놓고 싶은 역할이나 약속은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: What role or promise are you ready to gracefully step away from?
rows.en_before_tone: What role or commitment would you like to politely set down now?

rows.ko: 선 지키기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 기존의 부탁과 역할을 다 안고 가느라 새로운 시작에 쓸 자리가 부족해지기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 새 출발의 공간은 무엇을 더할지보다 무엇을 내려놓을지 정할 때 생겨나요.
rows.en: If saying no wears you out, you carry every old favor and role along with you, leaving little room for something new. {{기질문장}} Room for a fresh start opens the moment you decide what to release, not just what to add.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find holding boundaries draining can carry all their existing favors and roles so faithfully that there's little room left for a new start. {{기질문장}} Space for a fresh start opens up when you decide what to set down, more than what to add.

rows.ko: 마음을 놓기 위해 꺼내야 할 말은 무엇인가
rows.en: What do you need to say out loud so you can finally relax?
rows.en_before_tone: What do you need to say so you can feel at ease?

rows.ko: 하고 싶은 말을 삼킨 뒤 마음이 오래 불편했던 순간은 어떤 장면이었나요?
rows.en: Think of a time you held your tongue and felt uneasy about it long afterward.
rows.en_before_tone: What was a moment when you swallowed what you wanted to say and felt uneasy for a long time afterward?

rows.ko: 내 생각을 편하게 말할 수 있는 자리는 어디인가요?
rows.en: Where do you feel free to say what you think?
rows.en_before_tone: Where can you share your thoughts comfortably?

rows.ko: 안정을 위해 가까운 사람에게 미리 나누고 싶은 이야기는 무엇인가요?
rows.en: To feel more settled, what will you talk through with someone close before it becomes an issue?
rows.en_before_tone: For the sake of stability, what would you like to talk through with someone close ahead of time?

rows.ko: 말하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 갈등을 피하려고 말을 아끼다가 마음속 불안을 키우기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 안정을 바란다면, 하고 싶은 말을 작게라도 꺼내 두는 것이 오히려 관계를 단단하게 만들 수 있어요.
rows.en: When speaking up takes effort, holding back to avoid conflict lets worry build up inside. {{기질문장}} If stability is your wish, say what's on your mind, even in a small way. It makes your relationships stronger, not shakier.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find speaking up draining often hold back their words to avoid conflict, letting anxiety grow inside. {{기질문장}} If you're hoping for stability, saying what you want to say, even in a small way, can actually make relationships stronger.

rows.ko: 도약을 위해 꺼내 놓을 나의 목소리는 무엇인가
rows.en: What will you voice out loud to launch your leap?
rows.en_before_tone: What will you speak up about to make your leap?

rows.ko: 좋은 생각이 있었는데 말하지 않고 넘어간 회의나 대화는 어떤 장면이었나요?
rows.en: Recall a meeting or conversation where you had a good idea but let the moment pass.
rows.en_before_tone: What was a meeting or conversation where you had a good idea but let it pass without saying it?

rows.ko: 내가 하고 싶은 일을 한 문장으로 소개한다면 어떻게 말하고 싶나요?
rows.en: If you had to sum up what you want to do in one sentence, what would you say?
rows.en_before_tone: If you introduced what you want to do in one sentence, how would you say it?

rows.ko: 내 계획을 처음으로 들려주고 싶은 사람은 누구인가요?
rows.en: Who's the first person you'd like to tell about your plans?
rows.en_before_tone: Who would you like to tell about your plans first?

rows.ko: 말하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 준비가 다 될 때까지 생각을 꺼내지 않아 기회를 놓치기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 도약의 문은 완성된 결과보다, 하고 싶은 일을 먼저 말해 보는 데서 열리기도 해요.
rows.en: If speaking up is draining, you keep ideas to yourself until everything's perfect, and the moment slips by. {{기질문장}} The door to a big leap rarely opens with a finished result. It opens when you say out loud what you want to do, so say it first.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find speaking up draining often keep their ideas to themselves until everything is ready, and miss chances. {{기질문장}} The door to a leap sometimes opens not with a finished result, but with saying out loud what you want to do.

rows.ko: 지친 마음을 어떤 말로 꺼내 놓을 것인가
rows.en: How will you put into words just how tired you are?
rows.en_before_tone: What words will you use to share how worn out you feel?

rows.ko: 힘들다는 말 대신 ‘괜찮아’라고 답했던 순간은 어떤 장면이었나요?
rows.en: When was the last time you said 'I'm fine' when things were actually hard?
rows.en_before_tone: What was a moment when you said 'I'm fine' instead of saying things were hard?

rows.ko: 요즘 내 상태를 날씨로 표현한다면 어떤 날씨인가요?
rows.en: If your mood lately were a weather forecast, what would it be?
rows.en_before_tone: If you described how you've been lately as the weather, what kind of weather would it be?

rows.ko: 지친 마음을 털어놓을 때 들어 주는 사람에게 바라는 반응은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: When you open up about feeling worn out, what response do you want from the person listening?
rows.en_before_tone: When you open up about feeling worn out, how would you like the listener to respond?

rows.ko: 말하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 지쳐도 말로 꺼내지 못해 혼자 오래 버티기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 회복을 바란다면, 지금 상태를 한 문장으로라도 말해 보는 일이 쉬는 것만큼 중요한 열쇠가 될 수 있어요.
rows.en: When it's hard to speak up, you push through exhaustion alone for a long time without ever saying so. {{기질문장}} If recovery is your wish, name how you're doing, even in one sentence. Saying it matters as much as rest.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find speaking up draining often can't put their tiredness into words, so they hold on alone for a long time. {{기질문장}} If you're hoping to recover, describing how you are in even one sentence can be as important as rest.

rows.ko: 사랑하는 사람에게 아직 전하지 못한 말은 무엇인가
rows.en: What haven't you told someone you love yet?

rows.ko: 소중한 사람에게 서운했지만 말하지 않고 넘어간 순간은 어떤 장면이었나요?
rows.en: Think of a time someone dear hurt your feelings and you let it slide without a word.
rows.en_before_tone: What was a moment when someone dear hurt your feelings but you let it go without saying anything?

rows.ko: 고맙다거나 좋다는 마음을 표현할 때 나에게 가장 편한 방식은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: What's the easiest way for you to show thanks or affection?
rows.en_before_tone: What's the most comfortable way for you to express thanks or affection?

rows.ko: 가까운 사람에게 요즘 바라는 것을 부드럽게 말한다면 어떤 문장이 될까요?
rows.en: If you gently told someone close what you've been wishing for lately, what words would you choose?
rows.en_before_tone: If you gently told someone close what you've been hoping for lately, how might you put it?

rows.ko: 말하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 사랑하는 사이일수록 말하지 않아도 알아주길 바라기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 마음을 말로 건네는 작은 연습이 오해를 줄이고 사랑을 더 가깝게 느끼게 해 줄 수 있어요.
rows.en: Speaking up feels hardest with the people you love, where you hope they'll simply know. {{기질문장}} Practice putting your feelings into words, a little at a time. Misunderstandings fade, and love feels closer.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find speaking up draining often hope, especially with someone they love, to be understood without having to say it. {{기질문장}} A little practice putting your feelings into words can reduce misunderstandings and help love feel closer.

rows.ko: 좋은 사람들과 어떤 대화를 나누고 싶은가
rows.en: What kinds of conversations do you want to have with the good people in your life?
rows.en_before_tone: What kinds of conversations do you want to have with good people?

rows.ko: 대화가 잘 통해서 시간 가는 줄 몰랐던 순간은 어떤 장면이었나요?
rows.en: Recall a conversation that flowed so well you lost track of time.
rows.en_before_tone: What was a moment when a conversation flowed so well you lost track of time?

rows.ko: 여러 사람 사이에서 말을 꺼내기 망설여질 때 마음속에서는 어떤 생각이 드나요?
rows.en: When you hesitate to speak up in a group, what's running through your mind?
rows.en_before_tone: When you hesitate to speak up in a group, what thoughts go through your mind?

rows.ko: 가까운 사람들과 더 자주 나누고 싶은 이야기는 무엇인가요?
rows.en: What would you like to talk about more often with the people closest to you?
rows.en_before_tone: What would you like to talk about more often with the people close to you?

rows.ko: 말하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 듣는 쪽에 머물다 보니 관계가 깊어지기까지 시간이 걸리기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 좋은 사람들과의 관계는 내 이야기를 조금씩 나눌 때 서로를 알아 가며 자라나요.
rows.en: If speaking up takes effort, you settle into the role of listener, and your relationships take longer to deepen. {{기질문장}} Share a little more of your own story each time. That is how good people become kindred spirits.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find speaking up draining often stay in the listener's role, so relationships can take a while to deepen. {{기질문장}} Relationships with good people grow as you get to know each other, sharing a little of your own story at a time.

rows.ko: 여유를 위해 어떤 말을 미루지 않고 꺼낼 것인가
rows.en: What will you stop putting off saying, so you can breathe again?
rows.en_before_tone: What will you stop putting off saying, to make room to breathe?

rows.ko: ‘지금은 어려워’라는 말을 꺼내지 못해 일정이 빠듯해졌던 장면은 어떤 장면이었나요?
rows.en: Has your schedule ever filled up because you couldn't bring yourself to say 'Now isn't a good time'?
rows.en_before_tone: What was a time your schedule got tight because you couldn't say 'This doesn't work right now'?

rows.ko: 속에 담아 둔 말이 많을 때 마음은 어떤 상태가 되나요?
rows.en: When you're holding a lot inside, how does it feel?
rows.en_before_tone: How does your heart feel when you're holding a lot of things unsaid?

rows.ko: 여유를 위해 주변에 솔직하게 알리고 싶은 나의 사정은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: To give yourself breathing room, what about your situation will you be honest with people about?
rows.en_before_tone: To make room to breathe, what about your situation would you like to share honestly with people around you?

rows.ko: 말하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 상황을 설명하는 대신 혼자 감당하다가 여유를 잃기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 지금의 사정을 짧게라도 말로 알리는 것이 숨 돌릴 틈을 만드는 현실적인 방법이 될 수 있어요.
rows.en: When speaking up is a struggle, you shoulder everything alone instead of explaining what's going on, and your breathing room disappears. {{기질문장}} Let people know where things stand, even in a few words. It is the most practical way to make space to breathe.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find speaking up draining often handle things alone instead of explaining the situation, and lose their breathing room. {{기질문장}} Letting people know where things stand, even briefly, can be a practical way to make room to breathe.

rows.ko: 생활 리듬을 지키기 위해 어떤 말을 해 둘 것인가
rows.en: What will you say to protect your daily rhythm?

rows.ko: 피곤하다는 말을 삼키고 일정을 이어 갔던 날은 어떤 장면이었나요?
rows.en: Recall a day you pushed on with your plans instead of admitting 'I'm tired.'
rows.en_before_tone: What was a day when you kept going with your plans, swallowing the words 'I'm tired'?

rows.ko: 하루의 리듬을 지키기 위해 가족이나 동료에게 알려 두고 싶은 것은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: To protect your daily rhythm, what would you like your family or coworkers to know?
rows.en_before_tone: To keep your daily rhythm, what would you like to let family or coworkers know?

rows.ko: 새 습관을 시작할 때 누군가에게 소리 내어 말해 둔다면 어떤 문장이 좋을까요?
rows.en: When you start a new habit, what will you say out loud to someone about it?
rows.en_before_tone: When you start a new habit, what sentence would you like to say out loud to someone?

rows.ko: 말하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 피로나 필요를 말하지 않아 생활 리듬이 남의 일정에 끌려가기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 지키고 싶은 루틴을 주변에 말해 두면, 그 말이 습관을 이어 가는 약속이 되어 주기도 해요.
rows.en: If voicing your needs is hard, staying quiet about being tired leaves your routine at the mercy of other people's schedules. {{기질문장}} Tell the people around you about the routine you want to keep. Your words become a promise, and the habit sticks.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find speaking up draining often don't mention their tiredness or needs, so their daily rhythm gets pulled along by other people's schedules. {{기질문장}} When you tell people about a routine you want to keep, those words can become a promise that helps the habit last.

rows.ko: 돈에 관해 미뤄 둔 말은 무엇인가
rows.en: What have you been putting off saying about money?

rows.ko: 돈 이야기를 꺼내기 어려워 불편했던 장면은 어떤 것이었나요?
rows.en: Think of an awkward moment when money was hard to bring up.
rows.en_before_tone: What was an uncomfortable situation where money was hard to bring up?

rows.ko: 보수나 생활비처럼 말하기 어려운 돈 이야기를 한다면 누구와 먼저 나누고 싶나요?
rows.en: If you raised a tricky money topic, like pay or living costs, who would you go to first?
rows.en_before_tone: If you were to talk about a hard money topic, like pay or living costs, who would you want to talk to first?

rows.ko: 나에게 경제적 여유란 어떤 생활인지 한 문장으로 적는다면 어떤 문장이 될까요?
rows.en: In one sentence, what does financial ease look like in your life?
rows.en_before_tone: If you wrote down in one sentence what financial ease means for your life, what would it be?

rows.ko: 말하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 돈 이야기를 불편해하다가 필요한 요청이나 조정을 놓치기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 내 기준을 말로 정리해 보는 것만으로도 경제적 여유를 향한 길이 한결 또렷해질 수 있어요.
rows.en: When speaking up feels draining, money talk gets so uncomfortable that you miss the chance to ask for what you need or work things out. {{기질문장}} Put your own money rules into words. That simple act makes the path to financial ease much clearer.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find speaking up draining can feel so uncomfortable talking about money that they miss chances to make needed requests or adjustments. {{기질문장}} Just putting your standards into words can make the path toward financial ease much clearer.

rows.ko: 내가 해낸 일을 어떻게 말할 것인가
rows.en: How will you talk about what you've accomplished?

rows.ko: 열심히 한 일을 말하지 않아 아무도 몰랐던 순간은 어떤 장면이었나요?
rows.en: Recall something you worked hard on but never mentioned, so nobody knew.
rows.en_before_tone: What was a moment when you didn't mention something you worked hard on, so no one knew?

rows.ko: 내 성과를 자랑이 아니라 설명으로 전한다면 어떤 말로 시작하고 싶나요?
rows.en: If you shared your accomplishments as an explanation rather than a brag, how would you start?
rows.en_before_tone: If you shared your accomplishments as an explanation rather than bragging, how would you like to start?

rows.ko: 내 노력을 알리고 싶은 자리는 어디인가요?
rows.en: Where do you want your efforts to be seen?
rows.en_before_tone: Where would you like your efforts to be known?

rows.ko: 말하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 말하지 않아도 결과가 알려 주리라 믿고 기다리기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 인정을 바란다면, 내가 한 일을 담담하게 설명하는 연습이 생각보다 큰 차이를 만들 수 있어요.
rows.en: If speaking up is hard, you wait quietly and trust your results to speak for themselves. {{기질문장}} If recognition is your wish, practice explaining what you've done, calmly and plainly. It makes a bigger difference than you'd expect.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find speaking up draining often wait, trusting the results to speak for themselves. {{기질문장}} If you're hoping for recognition, practicing calmly explaining what you've done can make a bigger difference than you'd think.

rows.ko: 어떤 말을 할 때 가장 나다운가
rows.en: When do your words feel most like you?
rows.en_before_tone: When do you feel most like yourself in what you say?

rows.ko: 분위기에 맞추느라 내 생각과 다른 말을 했던 순간은 어떤 장면이었나요?
rows.en: Recall a time you said something you didn't really think, just to go along with the mood.
rows.en_before_tone: What was a moment when you said something different from what you thought, to fit the mood?

rows.ko: 말하고 나서 ‘이게 진짜 내 생각이야’라고 느꼈던 순간은 언제인가요?
rows.en: When have you spoken up and felt, 'Yes, this is what I really think'?
rows.en_before_tone: When was a moment you spoke and felt, 'This is what I really think'?

rows.ko: 조금 더 자주 말하고 싶은 나의 생각이나 취향은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: What opinions or tastes of yours deserve to be shared more often?
rows.en_before_tone: What thoughts or tastes of yours would you like to share a little more often?

rows.ko: 말하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 분위기를 살피다 보면 내 생각보다 무난한 말을 고르기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 나다움은 거창한 선언보다, 작은 대화 속에서 내 생각을 한 문장씩 꺼내는 데서 자라나요.
rows.en: When speaking up takes energy, reading the room leads you to choose safe words over your real thoughts. {{기질문장}} Being yourself grows less from grand declarations than from everyday conversations, where you voice your thoughts one sentence at a time.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find speaking up draining often read the room and pick safe words over their own thoughts. {{기질문장}} Being yourself grows less from big declarations and more from sharing your thoughts one sentence at a time in small conversations.

rows.ko: 새로운 시작을 어떤 말로 꺼낼 것인가
rows.en: How will you put a new beginning into words?
rows.en_before_tone: What words will you use to begin something new?

rows.ko: 해 보고 싶은 일이 있었지만 입 밖에 내지 못하고 넘어간 순간은 어떤 장면이었나요?
rows.en: Think of a time you wanted to try something but never said it out loud.
rows.en_before_tone: What was a moment when there was something you wanted to try, but you let it pass without saying it out loud?

rows.ko: 새로 배우거나 가 보고 싶은 길을 누군가에게 설명한다면 어떤 말로 시작하고 싶나요?
rows.en: If you told someone about something you'd love to learn or a path you'd like to explore, how would you begin?
rows.en_before_tone: If you explained to someone something new you'd like to learn or a path you'd like to take, how would you start?

rows.ko: 시작하고 싶은 일을 소리 내어 말해 두면 마음이 어떻게 달라질 것 같나요?
rows.en: Picture saying out loud what you want to start. How does that change the way you feel?
rows.en_before_tone: How do you think you'd feel if you said out loud what you want to start?

rows.ko: 말하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 새로운 시작도 확실해질 때까지 마음속에만 담아 두기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 하고 싶은 일을 먼저 말로 꺼내 두면, 그 말이 시작을 붙잡아 주는 첫 약속이 될 수 있어요.
rows.en: If speaking up is a struggle, you keep a new beginning to yourself until it feels certain. {{기질문장}} Say what you want to do out loud, early. Those words become your first promise, the one that keeps your fresh start from slipping away.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find speaking up draining often keep plans for a new start to themselves until it feels certain. {{기질문장}} Saying what you want to do out loud first can become the first promise that holds your start in place.

rows.ko: 어긋난 뒤에도 다시 이어질 수 있다는 믿음을 어떻게 쌓을 것인가
rows.en: How will you build faith that you can reconnect, even after things go wrong?
rows.en_before_tone: How will you build trust that you can reconnect even after things go wrong?

rows.ko: 다툰 뒤 다시 편해지기까지 시간이 오래 걸렸던 관계를 떠올리면, 무엇이 그 시간을 길게 만들었나요?
rows.en: Is there a relationship that took a long time to feel easy again after an argument? What made it take so long?
rows.en_before_tone: Think of a relationship where it took a long time to feel comfortable again after an argument. What made it take so long?

rows.ko: 갈등이 있었지만 오히려 가까워졌던 경험은 어떤 장면인가요?
rows.en: When has a conflict actually brought you closer to someone?
rows.en_before_tone: What's an experience where a conflict actually brought you closer?

rows.ko: 어긋났을 때 먼저 건넬 수 있는 짧은 한마디를 정해 둔다면 어떤 말일까요?
rows.en: Pick a short phrase you can say first when things go sideways. What will it be?
rows.en_before_tone: If you chose a short phrase you could offer first when things go wrong, what would it be?

rows.ko: 회복하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 작은 다툼에도 관계 전체가 흔들리는 것처럼 느끼기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 안정을 바란다면, 갈등이 없는 상태보다 어긋나도 다시 이어지는 경험을 쌓는 것이 열쇠가 될 수 있어요.
rows.en: When mending things takes a lot out of you, even a small argument feels like it's shaking the whole relationship. {{기질문장}} If stability is your wish, don't aim for zero conflict. Collect experiences of reconnecting after a rough patch; that is your real key.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find repairing draining often feel as if the whole relationship is shaken by even a small argument. {{기질문장}} If you're hoping for stability, the key may be building experiences of reconnecting after things go wrong, rather than having no conflict at all.

rows.ko: 부딪힘을 지나 더 나아가려면 무엇이 필요한가
rows.en: What do you need to get past a clash and keep moving forward?
rows.en_before_tone: What do you need to move past a clash and keep going?

rows.ko: 의견이 부딪힌 뒤 한동안 일에 집중하기 어려웠던 장면은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: Recall a time a disagreement left you struggling to focus on work for a while.
rows.en_before_tone: What was a time when, after a disagreement, you found it hard to focus on work for a while?

rows.ko: 피드백이나 반대 의견을 들은 뒤 다시 힘을 냈던 경험을 떠올리면, 무엇이 도움이 됐나요?
rows.en: Think of a time you bounced back after hearing feedback or pushback. What helped?
rows.en_before_tone: Think of a time you found your energy again after hearing feedback or disagreement. What helped?

rows.ko: 도전하며 생길 수 있는 마찰을 어떻게 다루고 싶나요?
rows.en: How will you handle the friction that comes with taking on challenges?
rows.en_before_tone: How would you like to handle the friction that may come up as you take on challenges?

rows.ko: 회복하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 갈등이 생길까 봐 새로운 도전 앞에서 한 발 물러서기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 도약에는 크고 작은 부딪힘이 함께 오기 쉬워서, 어긋난 뒤 다시 대화를 여는 힘이 앞으로 나아가는 바탕이 될 수 있어요.
rows.en: If repairing relationships is draining, worry about conflict makes you step back from new challenges. {{기질문장}} Big leaps come with bumps along the way. Your ability to reopen the conversation after a clash is the solid ground you move forward on.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find repairing draining often take a step back from new challenges, worried that conflict might arise. {{기질문장}} Leaps often come with bumps big and small, so the strength to reopen a conversation after things go wrong can be the ground you move forward on.

rows.ko: 마음에 남은 앙금을 어떻게 풀어낼 것인가
rows.en: How will you work through the hard feelings that linger?

rows.ko: 지난 다툼이 자꾸 떠올라 쉬는 시간에도 마음이 무거웠던 순간은 어떤 장면이었나요?
rows.en: Think of a time a past argument kept replaying in your mind and weighed on you even when you tried to rest.
rows.en_before_tone: What was a moment when a past argument kept coming back to you and weighed on you even while resting?

rows.ko: 아직 마음에 남아 있는 서운함을 떠올리면, 그 마음이 바라는 것은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: When you think of a hurt that still lingers, what does that feeling need?
rows.en_before_tone: When you think of hurt that still lingers in your heart, what is that feeling hoping for?

rows.ko: 관계를 다시 잇든 잠시 두든, 내 마음을 먼저 돌보기 위해 할 수 있는 일은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: Whether you reach out or give it time, what can you do to take care of yourself first?
rows.en_before_tone: Whether you reconnect or give it some time, what can you do to care for your own heart first?

rows.ko: 회복하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 풀리지 않은 갈등이 쉬는 동안에도 마음을 붙잡아 지치기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 회복을 바란다면, 관계를 바로 해결하는 것보다 내 마음에 남은 서운함부터 알아주는 일이 먼저일 수 있어요.
rows.en: For those who find repair hard, unresolved conflict keeps its grip even during downtime, and it wears you out. {{기질문장}} If recovery is your wish, acknowledge the hurt you're still carrying first. Fixing the relationship can come after.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find repairing draining often get worn out because unresolved conflict keeps a hold on their heart even while resting. {{기질문장}} If you're hoping to recover, acknowledging the hurt that lingers in your heart may come before fixing the relationship right away.

rows.ko: 사랑하는 사람과 어긋났을 때 어떻게 다시 다가갈 것인가
rows.en: When things go wrong with someone you love, how will you find your way back?
rows.en_before_tone: When things go wrong with someone you love, how will you reach out again?

rows.ko: 가까운 사람과 다툰 뒤 먼저 말을 걸기 어려웠던 순간은 어떤 장면이었나요?
rows.en: Recall a time after an argument with someone close when it felt hard to be the first to reach out.
rows.en_before_tone: What was a moment after an argument with someone close when it was hard to be the first to speak?

rows.ko: 화해했다고 느낀 순간, 상대와 나 사이에는 어떤 말이나 행동이 있었나요?
rows.en: When you felt you'd made up, what words or gestures passed between you?
rows.en_before_tone: When you felt you'd made up, what words or actions passed between you?

rows.ko: 어긋난 뒤 소중한 사람에게 건네고 싶은 다정한 한마디는 무엇인가요?
rows.en: After a falling-out, what kind words will you offer someone dear to you?
rows.en_before_tone: After things go wrong, what kind word would you like to offer someone dear to you?

rows.ko: 회복하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 사랑하는 사이일수록 다툼 뒤의 어색함을 오래 견디기 어렵습니다. {{기질문장}} 사랑을 바란다면, 다투지 않는 것보다 다툰 뒤 다시 다가가는 나만의 방식을 아는 것이 관계를 지켜 주는 힘이 될 수 있어요.
rows.en: If mending things is hard for you, the awkward silence after an argument is especially tough to sit with when it's someone you love. {{기질문장}} If love is your wish, learn your own way back after a fight. That, more than never fighting at all, is what keeps a relationship strong.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find repairing draining often find it hard to sit with the awkwardness after an argument, especially with someone they love. {{기질문장}} If you're hoping for love, knowing your own way of reaching out again after an argument, rather than never arguing, can be what protects the relationship.

rows.ko: 서운함이 생겨도 이어 가고 싶은 관계는 누구인가
rows.en: Which relationships are worth keeping, even when feelings get hurt?
rows.en_before_tone: Which relationships do you want to keep, even when hurt comes up?

rows.ko: 서운한 일 뒤에 자연스럽게 멀어진 관계를 떠올리면, 그때 전하지 못한 마음은 무엇이었나요?
rows.en: Picture a relationship that drifted apart after something hurtful. What did you leave unsaid?
rows.en_before_tone: Think of a relationship that quietly drifted apart after something hurtful. What did you leave unsaid then?

rows.ko: 작은 오해를 웃으며 풀었던 사람과의 장면은 어떤 모습이었나요?
rows.en: Recall a time you laughed off a small misunderstanding with someone. What was that like?
rows.en_before_tone: What was it like when you cleared up a small misunderstanding with someone over a laugh?

rows.ko: 다시 안부를 전해 보고 싶은 사람은 누구인가요?
rows.en: Who is it time to check in with again?
rows.en_before_tone: Who would you like to check in with again?

rows.ko: 회복하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 갈등이 생기면 관계를 조용히 정리하는 쪽을 택하기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 좋은 사람들은 어긋남이 없는 관계보다, 서운함을 지나 다시 이어진 관계에서 남는 경우가 많아요.
rows.en: When repairing feels draining, you tend to quietly let a relationship go once conflict shows up. {{기질문장}} The good people who stay in your life are rarely the ones you never clashed with. They are the ones you found your way back to after a hurt.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find repairing draining often choose to quietly let a relationship go when conflict comes up. {{기질문장}} The good people who stay in your life are often found not in relationships without bumps, but in ones that reconnected after hurt.

rows.ko: 풀리지 않은 갈등에 쓰는 마음을 어떻게 덜어 낼 것인가
rows.en: How will you stop pouring so much of yourself into unresolved conflict?
rows.en_before_tone: How will you spend less of your heart on unresolved conflict?

rows.ko: 지난 대화를 머릿속으로 계속 되짚느라 쉬지 못했던 밤은 어떤 장면이었나요?
rows.en: Recall a night you couldn't rest because you kept replaying an old conversation in your head.
rows.en_before_tone: What was a night you couldn't rest because you kept replaying a past conversation in your head?

rows.ko: 지금 당장 풀지 않아도 괜찮은 갈등을 떠올린다면 무엇이 생각나나요?
rows.en: What's a conflict that doesn't need to be sorted out right now?
rows.en_before_tone: When you think of a conflict that doesn't need to be resolved right now, what comes to mind?

rows.ko: 마음이 복잡할 때 생각을 잠시 내려놓게 해 주는 나만의 방법은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: When your mind is tangled, what's your go-to way to set your thoughts aside for a while?
rows.en_before_tone: What's your own way of setting your thoughts down for a while when your mind is tangled?

rows.ko: 회복하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 끝나지 않은 갈등을 머릿속으로 되풀이하느라 여유를 빼앗기기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 모든 어긋남을 당장 풀지 않아도 된다고 허락할 때, 마음에 숨 쉴 틈이 생길 수 있어요.
rows.en: If mending things takes effort, replaying unfinished conflicts in your head eats up your breathing room. {{기질문장}} Give yourself permission not to fix every misunderstanding right away, and you make room to breathe again.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find repairing draining often lose their breathing room replaying unfinished conflicts in their head. {{기질문장}} When you give yourself permission not to fix every misstep right away, your heart can find room to breathe.

rows.ko: 마음이 상한 날에도 지킬 생활의 리듬은 무엇인가
rows.en: What daily rhythm will you keep, even on days you're hurting?
rows.en_before_tone: What daily rhythm will you keep, even on days your feelings are hurt?

rows.ko: 누군가와 다툰 날, 잠이나 식사 같은 생활 리듬은 어떻게 달라졌나요?
rows.en: On a day you argued with someone, how did your routine, like sleep or meals, change?
rows.en_before_tone: On a day you argued with someone, how did your daily rhythm, like sleep or meals, change?

rows.ko: 속상한 일이 있어도 꼭 지키고 싶은 하루의 습관은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: What daily habit do you want to keep even when something upsets you?
rows.en_before_tone: What daily habit do you want to keep, even when something upsets you?

rows.ko: 마음이 어수선한 날 나를 다시 일상으로 데려와 주는 작은 루틴은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: On a day your mind is all over the place, what small routine brings you back to normal?
rows.en_before_tone: On a day your mind feels scattered, what small routine brings you back to everyday life?

rows.ko: 회복하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 관계가 어긋나면 잠과 식사 같은 생활 리듬까지 함께 흔들리기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 감정이 출렁이는 날에도 지킬 작은 루틴을 정해 두면, 마음이 돌아올 자리가 생겨요.
rows.en: When repair is hard for you, a rift in a relationship throws off your basics too, like sleep and meals. {{기질문장}} Choose one small routine to keep even on emotional days. It becomes the steady place you come back to.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find repairing draining often find that when a relationship goes off track, their daily rhythm, like sleep and meals, gets shaken too. {{기질문장}} Choosing a small routine to keep even on emotional days gives your heart a place to come back to.

rows.ko: 돈 때문에 생긴 불편함을 어떻게 풀어 갈 것인가
rows.en: How will you work through the awkwardness money has caused?
rows.en_before_tone: How will you work through discomfort caused by money?

rows.ko: 돈 문제로 가까운 사람과 서먹해졌던 장면을 떠올리면, 그때 가장 불편했던 것은 무엇이었나요?
rows.en: Think of a time money made things awkward with someone close. What bothered you most?
rows.en_before_tone: Think of a time money made things awkward with someone close. What felt most uncomfortable then?

rows.ko: 돈 이야기로 생긴 오해를 풀 때 어떤 방식이 서로에게 편할까요?
rows.en: When you clear up a misunderstanding about money, what approach feels comfortable for you both?
rows.en_before_tone: When clearing up a misunderstanding about money, what approach would feel comfortable for both of you?

rows.ko: 생활비나 지출에 대해 미리 나눠 두면 마음이 편해질 기준은 무엇일까요?
rows.en: What ground rules for spending or living costs, agreed on in advance, would put your mind at ease?
rows.en_before_tone: What standards for living costs or spending, agreed on ahead of time, would help you feel at ease?

rows.ko: 회복하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 돈 문제로 생긴 어색함을 꺼내지 못하고 오래 품기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 경제적 여유는 금액만의 문제가 아니라, 돈 이야기를 편하게 나누고 정리할 수 있는 관계에서도 자라요.
rows.en: If repairing things is draining, you carry money-related awkwardness for a long time without bringing it up. {{기질문장}} Financial ease isn't only about the numbers. It also grows in relationships where you talk about money openly and sort things out together.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find repairing draining often hold on to awkwardness about money for a long time without bringing it up. {{기질문장}} Financial ease isn't only about the amount. It also grows in relationships where you can talk about and sort out money comfortably.

rows.ko: 서운한 평가 뒤에 어떻게 다시 일어설 것인가
rows.en: How will you bounce back after feedback that stung?
rows.en_before_tone: How will you get back up after feedback that hurt?

rows.ko: 지적이나 비판을 들은 뒤 한동안 마음이 가라앉았던 장면은 어떤 것이었나요?
rows.en: Recall a time you felt down for a while after being corrected or criticized.
rows.en_before_tone: What was a time when you felt low for a while after being corrected or criticized?

rows.ko: 서운한 평가를 받은 뒤에도 관계를 잘 이어 갔던 경험을 떠올리면, 무엇이 도움이 됐나요?
rows.en: Think of a time you kept a relationship on good terms even after feedback that hurt. What helped?
rows.en_before_tone: Think of a time you kept a relationship going well even after hurtful feedback. What helped?

rows.ko: 나를 인정해 주었으면 하는 사람과 어떤 대화를 나누고 싶나요?
rows.en: What conversation do you want to have with someone whose recognition matters to you?
rows.en_before_tone: What kind of conversation would you like to have with someone you hope will recognize you?

rows.ko: 회복하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 인정받고 싶은 마음이 클수록 비판 한마디에 오래 흔들리기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 어긋난 평가 뒤에도 다시 대화를 이어 가는 힘이 쌓일 때, 인정은 더 단단한 신뢰로 돌아올 수 있어요.
rows.en: When repair takes effort, the more you want recognition, the longer a single critical comment stays with you. {{기질문장}} Keep the conversation going even after an unfair review. As that strength builds, recognition returns to you as deeper trust.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find repairing draining can be shaken for a long time by a single critical remark, especially when they want recognition. {{기질문장}} As you build the strength to keep talking even after an evaluation that missed the mark, recognition can come back as deeper trust.

rows.ko: 갈등 앞에서도 나답게 남는 방법은 무엇인가
rows.en: How will you stay true to yourself, even in conflict?
rows.en_before_tone: How can you stay yourself, even in conflict?

rows.ko: 갈등을 빨리 끝내려고 내 마음과 다르게 물러섰던 순간은 어떤 장면이었나요?
rows.en: Think of a time you backed down against your own feelings just to end a conflict quickly.
rows.en_before_tone: What was a moment when you backed down against your own feelings just to end a conflict quickly?

rows.ko: 다툰 뒤에도 내 마음을 솔직하게 전한다면 어떤 말로 시작하고 싶나요?
rows.en: If you shared your feelings honestly after an argument, how would you like to begin?
rows.en_before_tone: If you shared your feelings honestly after an argument, how would you like to start?

rows.ko: 관계를 지키면서도 나를 잃지 않았다고 느낀 경험은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: When have you protected a relationship without losing yourself?
rows.en_before_tone: What's an experience where you felt you protected a relationship without losing yourself?

rows.ko: 회복하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 관계를 되돌리려다 내 마음을 뒤로 미루기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 나다움은 갈등을 피하는 데서가 아니라, 어긋난 뒤에도 내 마음을 지키며 다시 다가가는 방식에서 드러나요.
rows.en: If mending things wears you out, you push your own feelings aside in the rush to set things right. {{기질문장}} Being yourself shows not in avoiding conflict, but in how you reach out again after a rift while still honoring what you feel.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find repairing draining often put their own feelings aside while trying to mend a relationship. {{기질문장}} Being yourself shows not in avoiding conflict, but in how you reach out again after things go wrong while still honoring your own heart.

rows.ko: 새로운 시작 앞에서 생기는 엇갈림을 어떻게 다룰 것인가
rows.en: How will you handle the disagreements that come with a fresh start?
rows.en_before_tone: How will you handle the differences that come up with a new start?

rows.ko: 새로운 선택을 했을 때 가까운 사람과 생각이 엇갈렸던 장면은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: Recall a time you made a new choice and someone close saw it differently. What happened?
rows.en_before_tone: Think of a time you made a new choice and saw things differently from someone close. What was that like?

rows.ko: 내 결정을 이해받지 못했을 때도 관계를 이어 갔던 경험을 떠올리면, 무엇이 도움이 됐나요?
rows.en: Think of a time you kept a relationship going even when someone didn't understand your decision. What helped?
rows.en_before_tone: Think of a time you kept a relationship going even when your decision wasn't understood. What helped?

rows.ko: 새 출발을 앞두고 소중한 사람에게 미리 건네고 싶은 말은 무엇인가요?
rows.en: As your fresh start approaches, what will you say to someone dear beforehand?
rows.en_before_tone: As you head toward a fresh start, what would you like to say to someone dear ahead of time?

rows.ko: 회복하기에 에너지가 드는 사람은 누군가 서운해할까 봐 새로운 시작을 망설이기 쉽습니다. {{기질문장}} 새 출발에는 작은 엇갈림이 따르기 쉬워서, 어긋난 뒤 다시 마음을 잇는 힘이 시작을 지켜 주는 바탕이 될 수 있어요.
rows.en: When repairing is hard, worry that someone will feel hurt makes you hesitate to start something new. {{기질문장}} New beginnings bring small disagreements. Trust your ability to reconnect after a misstep; it is what protects your fresh start.
rows.en_before_tone: People who find repairing draining often hesitate to start something new, worried someone might feel hurt. {{기질문장}} A fresh start often comes with small differences, so the strength to reconnect after things go wrong can be what protects your start.

A17b.name: 기질 문장 (태양 원소 × 달 원소)
A17b.used_in: 캐릭터 섹션 태양·달 대비 문단, 7번 섹션 ‘왜 이 질문인지’의 기질 문장

rows.ko: 불
rows.en: Fire
rows.note: 원소 단일 값 — 코드에서 키로 쓰이면 한국어 키 유지

rows.ko: 불
rows.en: Fire
rows.note: 원소 단일 값 — 코드에서 키로 쓰이면 한국어 키 유지

rows.ko: 겉은 빠르고 당당한 {{태양별자리}} 태양이고, 속도 마음이 움직이면 바로 표현하고 싶은 {{달별자리}} 달이에요. 겉과 속이 같은 방향으로 달리기 때문에 시작하는 힘이 크지만, 쉬어 가는 타이밍은 따로 챙겨야 할 수 있습니다.
rows.en: Your {{태양별자리}} Sun is quick and confident, and your {{달별자리}} Moon shows what it feels the second it feels it. With your outer and inner self racing in the same direction, you have boundless get-up-and-go. Schedule your downtime on purpose, because it won't arrive on its own.
rows.en_before_tone: On the outside, you're a quick, confident {{태양별자리}} Sun, and on the inside, a {{달별자리}} Moon that wants to express feelings the moment they stir. Because your outside and inside run in the same direction, you have a strong drive to start things, but you may need to make a point of finding times to rest.

rows.ko: 겉도 속도 빠르게 불붙는 기질이라 멈추는 연습이 따로 필요할 수 있어요.
rows.en: You catch fire fast, inside and out, so make pausing a skill you practice on purpose.
rows.en_before_tone: Your temperament catches fire quickly, outside and in, so you may need to practice pausing on purpose.

rows.ko: 불
rows.en: Fire
rows.note: 원소 단일 값 — 코드에서 키로 쓰이면 한국어 키 유지

rows.ko: 흙
rows.en: Earth
rows.note: 원소 단일 값 — 코드에서 키로 쓰이면 한국어 키 유지

rows.ko: 겉은 빠르고 당당한 {{태양별자리}} 태양이지만, 속은 차근차근 정리해야 편한 {{달별자리}} 달이에요. 가끔 일단 저지르고 나서 혼자 계속 점검하는 자신을 발견한다면, 이 두 기운의 차이 때문일 수 있습니다.
rows.en: Outwardly, you're a quick, confident {{태양별자리}} Sun. Inside, your {{달별자리}} Moon is happiest when things are sorted step by step. If you often leap first and then quietly double-check everything afterward, you're feeling the push and pull between these two energies.
rows.en_before_tone: On the outside, you're a quick, confident {{태양별자리}} Sun, but on the inside, a {{달별자리}} Moon that feels at ease when things are sorted step by step. If you sometimes catch yourself jumping in first and then double-checking everything on your own, it may come from the difference between these two energies.

rows.ko: 먼저 움직이는 겉과 하나하나 점검해야 마음이 놓이는 속이 함께 있는 기질입니다.
rows.en: You act first on the outside, yet inside you relax only once you've checked every detail.
rows.en_before_tone: Your temperament combines an outside that moves first with an inside that feels at ease only after checking things one by one.

rows.ko: 불
rows.en: Fire
rows.note: 원소 단일 값 — 코드에서 키로 쓰이면 한국어 키 유지

rows.ko: 공기
rows.en: Air
rows.note: 원소 단일 값 — 코드에서 키로 쓰이면 한국어 키 유지

rows.ko: 겉은 빠르고 당당한 {{태양별자리}} 태양이고, 속은 생각을 말로 정리해야 편한 {{달별자리}} 달이에요. 불과 공기는 서로를 키우는 사이라 생각이 금세 행동으로 이어지지만, 감정은 한 걸음 떨어져 정리할 시간이 필요할 수 있습니다.
rows.en: The world sees a quick, confident {{태양별자리}} Sun, while your {{달별자리}} Moon settles once it puts its thoughts into words. Fire and Air fuel each other, so your ideas turn into action fast. Give your feelings a little time and distance to catch up.
rows.en_before_tone: On the outside, you're a quick, confident {{태양별자리}} Sun, and on the inside, a {{달별자리}} Moon that feels at ease when thoughts are sorted into words. Fire and Air feed each other, so ideas quickly turn into action, but your feelings may need some time and a little distance to sort themselves out.

rows.ko: 빠르게 움직이면서도 마음은 한 발 떨어져 생각으로 정리하려는 기질이에요.
rows.en: You move fast, yet inside you like to step back and think things through.
rows.en_before_tone: Your temperament moves quickly, while your heart likes to step back and think things through.

rows.ko: 불
rows.en: Fire
rows.note: 원소 단일 값 — 코드에서 키로 쓰이면 한국어 키 유지

rows.ko: 물
rows.en: Water
rows.note: 원소 단일 값 — 코드에서 키로 쓰이면 한국어 키 유지

rows.ko: 겉은 빠르고 당당한 {{태양별자리}} 태양이지만, 속은 감정을 깊이 느끼고 마음이 통해야 편한 {{달별자리}} 달이에요. 씩씩하게 앞장서다가도 혼자 있을 때 작은 말 한마디를 오래 곱씹는다면, 이 두 기운의 차이 때문일 수 있습니다.
rows.en: You come across as a quick, confident {{태양별자리}} Sun, but your {{달별자리}} Moon feels things deeply and needs real emotional closeness to feel at ease. If you lead the charge in public yet replay one small comment for hours once you're alone, these two contrasting energies are at play.
rows.en_before_tone: On the outside, you're a quick, confident {{태양별자리}} Sun, but on the inside, a {{달별자리}} Moon that feels deeply and is at ease when hearts connect. If you lead boldly but then turn a small comment over in your mind for a long time when you're alone, it may come from the difference between these two energies.

rows.ko: 씩씩하게 앞장서는 겉과 작은 말에도 깊이 흔들리는 속이 함께 있는 기질입니다.
rows.en: You lead boldly on the outside, while inside, even a few small words linger for a long time.
rows.en_before_tone: Your temperament combines a bold outside that leads the way with an inside that can be deeply moved by small words.

rows.ko: 흙

rows.en: Sea Otter
rows.note: 캐릭터명

rows.ko: 힘든 날에도 상대 기분부터 살피고 내 이야기는 뒤로 미루는 습관은 내려놓아 볼 만해요. 한때 관계를 편안하게 지켜 준 고마운 방법이었지만, 계속 미루다 보면 정작 내가 기댈 자리가 줄어들기 때문입니다.
rows.en: Even on hard days, you check on how others feel and save your own story for later. Set that habit down. It once kept your relationships comfortable, but the longer you put yourself last, the fewer places you have to lean on.
rows.en_before_tone: The habit of checking how others feel first and pushing your own story aside, even on hard days, is worth setting down. It was once a kind way of keeping relationships comfortable, but if you keep putting yourself last, you may find fewer places to lean on.

rows.ko: 내 이야기도 누군가에게 기대어 꺼내도 괜찮다고 믿는 힘을 키울 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 대화할 때마다 한 번은, 오늘 내 기분이 어땠는지 먼저 꺼내 보세요.
rows.en: Next, you build the trust that it's safe to lean on someone and share your story too. In the year ahead, be the first to say how your day went at least once in every conversation.
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your trust that it's okay to lean on someone and share your story too. In the year ahead, try, at least once in every conversation, being the first to share how you felt today.

rows.ko: 물범
rows.en: Seal
rows.note: 캐릭터명 — 물범(harbor seal); 필요시 Harbor Seal

rows.ko: 다 정리된 뒤에야 지나간 일처럼 털어놓는 습관은 조금 느슨하게 풀어도 괜찮습니다. 혼자 추스르는 시간은 한때 나를 단단하게 지켜 준 방법이지만, 그사이 곁에 있는 사람이 도울 기회도 함께 지나가기 때문이에요.
rows.en: Stop waiting until everything's sorted to open up and talk about it like old news. Pulling yourself together alone once kept you strong, but while you do, the people around you lose their chance to help.
rows.en_before_tone: It's okay to loosen the habit of opening up only after everything is sorted, as if it were all in the past. Taking time to pull yourself together alone once kept you steady, but in the meantime, the chance for the people around you to help slips by too.

rows.ko: 정리가 덜 된 마음도 가까운 사람에게 보여 줄 수 있는 힘을 키울 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 힘든 일이 생긴 그 주 안에, 믿는 한 사람에게 요즘 이런 일이 있다고만 먼저 알려 보세요.
rows.en: Your growth edge now is letting someone close see your feelings, even while they're still messy. In the year ahead, the same week something hard happens, tell one person you trust, "Here's what's been going on lately."
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your ability to show even unsorted feelings to someone close. In the year ahead, in the same week something hard happens, try simply letting one person you trust know, "This is what's been going on lately."

rows.ko: 비버
rows.en: Beaver
rows.note: 캐릭터명

rows.ko: 속상한 날일수록 할 일만 붙잡고 바쁘게 움직이는 습관은 내려놓아도 돼요. 눈앞의 일을 정리하는 힘은 한때 흔들리는 하루를 붙잡아 준 방법이지만, 마음을 나눌 틈까지 일로 채우면 혼자 지치기 쉽기 때문입니다.
rows.en: On upset days, you grab your to-do list and keep yourself busy. Let that habit go. Focusing on the task at hand once held shaky days together, but when work fills every gap, even the time you could spend opening up, you wear yourself out alone.
rows.en_before_tone: You can set down the habit of clinging to your to-do list and keeping busy, especially on days you're upset. Sorting out what's in front of you once helped hold a shaky day together, but if you fill even the space for sharing your feelings with tasks, you can easily wear yourself out alone.

rows.ko: 계획보다 마음을 먼저 꺼내 기대는 힘을 키워 볼 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 함께할 일을 정하기 전에, 요즘 어떤 기분인지 서로 한 번씩 묻는 시간을 만들어 보세요.
rows.en: Now you learn to lean on people by sharing how you feel before you share your plans. In the year ahead, before deciding what to do together, make a ritual of asking each other how you've really been.
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your ability to lean on others by sharing your feelings before your plans. In the year ahead, before deciding what to do together, try making time to ask each other how you've been feeling lately.

rows.ko: 원앙
rows.en: Mandarin Duck
rows.note: 캐릭터명 — 원앙(금슬 좋은 부부의 상징)은 영어권에서 그런 함의가 약함

rows.ko: 확인을 받고도 다시 묻고 싶어지는 마음은 조금씩 내려놓아 볼 만해요. 먼저 다가가 마음을 확인하는 일은 한때 관계를 지켜 준 방법이지만, 답을 자주 구할수록 오히려 불안이 길어지기 쉽기 때문입니다.
rows.en: Little by little, release the urge to ask again even after you've been reassured. Reaching out to check where you stand once protected your relationships, but the more often you seek reassurance, the longer the anxiety lingers.
rows.en_before_tone: The urge to ask again even after you've been reassured is worth setting down, little by little. Reaching out first to check how someone feels once protected your relationships, but the more often you seek answers, the longer the anxiety tends to last.

rows.ko: 말로 확인하지 않아도 함께 쌓아 온 시간을 믿는 힘을 키울 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 묻고 싶은 마음이 올라올 때마다 고마웠던 순간을 하나씩 적어 두는 작은 기록을 시작해 보세요.
rows.en: Your next step is to trust the time you've built together, without needing to hear it in words. In the year ahead, start a small journal: each time the urge to ask rises, write down one moment you felt grateful for.
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your trust in the time you've built together, even without checking in words. In the year ahead, try keeping a small record: each time the urge to ask comes up, write down one moment you were grateful for.

rows.ko: 펭귄
rows.en: Penguin
rows.note: 캐릭터명

rows.ko: 사이가 틀어질까 봐 서운한 마음까지 삼키는 습관은 내려놓아도 괜찮아요. 상대에게 맞춰 주는 마음은 한때 소중한 사이를 지켜 준 방법이지만, 참은 서운함이 쌓이면 오히려 믿음이 얇아지기 때문입니다.
rows.en: Stop swallowing your hurt feelings out of fear of rocking the boat. Going along with others once protected the relationships you cherish, but when hurt piles up unspoken, trust starts to wear thin.
rows.en_before_tone: It's okay to set down the habit of swallowing even your hurt feelings for fear of things going wrong between you. Going along with others once protected relationships that mattered to you, but when held-back hurt piles up, trust can actually wear thin.

rows.ko: 내가 원하는 것을 말해도 관계가 쉽게 무너지지 않는다고 믿는 힘을 키워 볼 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 메뉴나 약속 장소처럼 작은 선택부터 내 의견을 먼저 내 보세요.
rows.en: Now you build the confidence that saying what you want won't make a relationship crumble. In the year ahead, start small: pick the restaurant or the meeting spot, and speak up first.
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your trust that a relationship won't easily fall apart when you say what you want. In the year ahead, try starting with small choices, like the menu or where to meet, and sharing your opinion first.

rows.ko: 왜가리
rows.en: Heron
rows.note: 캐릭터명

rows.ko: 믿어도 될지 끝까지 확인한 뒤에야 마음을 여는 습관은 조금 풀어 놓아도 돼요. 멀리서 지켜보는 신중함은 한때 상처를 막아 준 방법이지만, 확인이 길어지면 이미 다가온 따뜻함을 놓치기 쉽기 때문입니다.
rows.en: Relax the habit of opening up only once you're completely sure someone can be trusted. Watching carefully from a distance once spared you from getting hurt, but when the vetting drags on, you miss warmth that's already right in front of you.
rows.en_before_tone: You can loosen the habit of opening up only after you've fully confirmed you can trust someone. Careful watching from a distance once protected you from hurt, but when the checking goes on too long, you can miss the warmth that's already come your way.

rows.ko: 모든 것이 확인되지 않아도 조금씩 마음을 맡겨 보는 힘을 키울 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 지켜보던 사람 가운데 한 명에게 작은 고민 하나를 먼저 나눠 보세요.
rows.en: Your moment has come to trust people a little at a time, even before everything checks out. In the year ahead, choose one of the people you've been watching from afar and share a small worry with them first.
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your ability to entrust your heart little by little, even when not everything is confirmed. In the year ahead, try sharing one small worry first with one of the people you've been watching from afar.

rows.ko: 백조
rows.en: Swan
rows.note: 캐릭터명

rows.ko: 불안한 마음은 숨긴 채 혼자 대비책만 다시 짜는 습관은 내려놓아 볼 만해요. 속으로 균형을 잡는 힘은 한때 관계를 흔들림 없이 지켜 준 방법이지만, 혼자 감당하는 무게가 커질수록 쉽게 지치기 때문입니다.
rows.en: Release the habit of hiding your worries and quietly redrawing backup plans on your own. Keeping your balance on the inside once held your relationships steady, but the more you carry alone, the faster you wear out.
rows.en_before_tone: The habit of hiding your anxiety and quietly redrawing backup plans on your own is worth setting down. The ability to keep your balance inside once kept your relationships steady, but the heavier the weight you carry alone, the more easily you tire.

rows.ko: 불안을 말로 나눠도 관계가 단단히 버틴다고 믿는 힘을 키워 볼 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 계획을 세우기 전에, 요즘 마음에 걸리는 점을 가까운 사람과 먼저 나눠 보세요.
rows.en: Your next chapter is about trusting that a relationship holds steady even when you voice your worries. In the year ahead, before you make plans, tell someone close what's been weighing on you.
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your trust that a relationship can hold firm even when you share your worries out loud. In the year ahead, before making plans, try first sharing what's been on your mind with someone close.

rows.ko: 복어
rows.en: Pufferfish
rows.note: 캐릭터명

rows.ko: 불편함이 느껴지는 순간 바로 세게 맞서는 습관은 조금 내려놓아도 괜찮아요. 즉시 신호를 보내는 힘은 한때 나를 지켜 준 방법이지만, 말이 앞서면 정말 지키고 싶던 것이 오히려 가려지기 때문입니다.
rows.en: Tone down the reflex to push back hard the second something feels off. Sending a signal right away once protected you, but when the words rush out too fast, they hide the very thing you meant to protect.
rows.en_before_tone: It's okay to loosen the habit of pushing back hard the moment something feels uncomfortable. Sending a signal right away once protected you, but when words rush out first, what you really wanted to protect can get hidden.

rows.ko: 내가 원하는 선을 차분한 말로 분명하게 전하는 힘을 키울 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 자주 불편해지는 상황 하나를 골라, 그때 할 말을 미리 한 문장으로 준비해 두세요.
rows.en: You're ready to state your boundaries clearly and calmly. In the year ahead, pick one situation that keeps making you uncomfortable and have one sentence ready for the next time it happens.
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your ability to share your boundaries clearly in calm words. In the year ahead, try picking one situation that often makes you uncomfortable and preparing one sentence to say when it happens.

rows.ko: 소라게
rows.en: Hermit Crab
rows.note: 캐릭터명

rows.ko: 싫다는 말을 삼키고 부탁부터 들어주는 습관은 내려놓아 볼 만해요. 상대에게 맞춰 자리를 내주는 마음은 한때 관계를 부드럽게 지켜 준 방법이지만, 계속되면 내게 맞는 자리를 잃기 쉽기 때문입니다.
rows.en: Drop the habit of swallowing your 'no' and agreeing to favors before anything else. Making room for others once kept your relationships smooth, but if it goes on, you lose the space that's truly yours.
rows.en_before_tone: The habit of swallowing your 'no' and saying yes to favors first is worth setting down. Making room for others once kept relationships smooth, but if it goes on, you can lose the space that truly fits you.

rows.ko: 다정함은 지키면서 내 몫과 남의 몫을 구분하는 힘을 키울 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 부탁을 받으면 바로 답하지 말고, 생각해 보고 알려 주겠다는 말로 시간을 벌어 보세요.
rows.en: Your growth now is keeping your kindness while getting clear on what's yours to handle and what isn't. In the year ahead, when someone asks a favor, don't answer on the spot. Buy yourself time with "Let me think about it and get back to you."
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your ability to tell your share apart from others', while keeping your kindness. In the year ahead, when someone asks a favor, try not to answer right away. You might buy yourself time by saying you'll think about it and get back to them.

rows.ko: 거북
rows.en: Turtle
rows.note: 캐릭터명

rows.ko: 불편하다는 말 대신 조용히 연락을 줄이고 물러나는 습관은 조금 풀어 놓아도 돼요. 혼자 숨을 고르는 시간은 한때 나를 지켜 준 안전한 방법이지만, 이유를 모르는 상대는 같은 선을 또 넘기 쉽기 때문입니다.
rows.en: When something bothers you, you quietly text less and pull away. Loosen that habit. Retreating to catch your breath once kept you safe, but if the other person never learns why, they cross the same line again.
rows.en_before_tone: You can loosen the habit of quietly reaching out less and pulling away instead of saying something feels uncomfortable. Time alone to catch your breath once kept you safe, but someone who doesn't know why may easily cross the same line again.

rows.ko: 물러나기 전에 어디까지가 편한지 말로 알려 주는 힘을 키울 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 불편한 일이 생기면 짧은 메시지로라도 내가 바라는 것을 하나 전해 보세요.
rows.en: Now you practice telling people what you're comfortable with before you pull back. In the year ahead, when something bothers you, share one thing you'd like, even in a short text.
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your ability to put into words what you're comfortable with before pulling away. In the year ahead, when something uncomfortable happens, try sharing one thing you'd like, even in a short message.

rows.ko: 조개
rows.en: Clam
rows.note: 캐릭터명

rows.ko: 어디까지 보여 줄지 매번 계산하느라 내 마음을 뒤로 미루는 습관은 내려놓아도 괜찮아요. 신중하게 가늠하는 힘은 한때 나를 지켜 준 든든한 방법이지만, 따지는 데 힘을 다 쓰면 정작 내가 원하는 것을 놓치기 때문입니다.
rows.en: Stop putting your own feelings last while you calculate, every single time, how much of yourself to show. Weighing things carefully once kept you safe, but when all your energy goes into the math, you lose sight of what you actually want.
rows.en_before_tone: It's okay to set down the habit of putting your own feelings last because you're always calculating how much to show. Careful judgment once kept you safe, but if you spend all your energy weighing things, you miss what you actually want.

rows.ko: 계산보다 내 마음을 먼저 확인하고 선을 정하는 힘을 키울 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 한 주를 돌아보며 편했던 만남과 지쳤던 만남을 나눠 적고, 그 차이로 나만의 기준을 세워 보세요.
rows.en: Check in with how you feel first, before you start calculating, and set your boundaries from there. In the year ahead, look back on each week, jot down which get-togethers felt easy and which drained you, and let that difference shape your own ground rules.
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your ability to check your own heart first, before calculating, and set your boundaries from there. In the year ahead, try looking back on each week, writing down which get-togethers felt comfortable and which wore you out, and using the difference to set your own standards.

rows.ko: 물개
rows.en: Fur Seal
rows.note: 캐릭터명 — 물개(fur seal)와 물범(seal) 구분 유지

rows.ko: 떠오른 말을 그 자리에서 바로 꺼내야 마음이 놓이는 습관은 조금 내려놓아 볼 만해요. 먼저 목소리를 내는 힘은 한때 대화를 열어 준 방법이지만, 급하게 나간 말은 뒤늦게 곱씹을 일을 남기기 쉽기 때문입니다.
rows.en: Loosen the need to say whatever pops into your head the instant it arrives. Speaking up first once got conversations going, but words that rush out leave you replaying them later.
rows.en_before_tone: The habit of needing to say whatever comes to mind right away to feel at ease is worth loosening a little. Speaking up first once opened up conversations, but words that rush out often leave you turning them over later.

rows.ko: 하고 싶은 말을 상대에게 잘 닿도록 다듬어 전하는 힘을 키울 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 중요한 대화를 마친 뒤 상대가 어떻게 들었는지 한 번 물어보는 습관을 들여 보세요.
rows.en: Now you hone what you say so it truly lands with the other person. In the year ahead, after an important conversation, ask how it came across, and make that a habit.
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your ability to shape what you want to say so it really reaches the other person. In the year ahead, try making a habit of asking, after an important conversation, how the other person heard it.

rows.ko: 돌고래
rows.en: Dolphin
rows.note: 캐릭터명

rows.ko: 분위기를 살리느라 내 생각을 뒤로 숨기는 습관은 내려놓아도 괜찮아요. 맞장구로 대화를 밝게 만드는 힘은 한때 모두를 편하게 해 준 방법이지만, 계속되면 내 목소리가 대화에서 점점 옅어지기 때문입니다.
rows.en: Stop hiding what you really think just to keep the mood light. Chiming in to brighten a conversation once put everyone at ease, but if it goes on, your own voice slowly fades from the room.
rows.en_before_tone: It's okay to set down the habit of hiding your thoughts to keep the mood up. Brightening conversations by chiming in once made everyone comfortable, but if it continues, your own voice can slowly fade from the conversation.

rows.ko: 분위기는 지키면서 내 진짜 생각을 한 문장 보태는 힘을 키울 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 가까운 사람과의 대화부터, 나는 조금 다르게 생각했다는 말을 편하게 꺼내 보세요.
rows.en: Your next step is keeping the warm mood going while adding one sentence of what you really think. In the year ahead, start with the people closest to you, and get comfortable saying, "I actually see it a little differently."
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your ability to add one sentence of what you really think while keeping the mood. In the year ahead, starting with conversations with people close to you, try comfortably saying, "I saw it a little differently."

rows.ko: 혹등고래
rows.en: Humpback Whale
rows.note: 캐릭터명

rows.ko: 완벽하게 다듬어질 때까지 말을 품고 있는 습관은 조금 풀어 놓아도 돼요. 깊이 생각하는 시간은 한때 후회할 말을 막아 준 방법이지만, 다듬는 사이 말할 때가 지나가 버리기 쉽기 때문입니다.
rows.en: Loosen your hold on words you keep back until they're perfectly polished. Taking time to think deeply once kept you from saying things you'd regret, but while you polish, the moment to speak slips away.
rows.en_before_tone: You can loosen the habit of holding on to your words until they're perfectly polished. Time spent thinking deeply once kept you from saying things you'd regret, but while you're polishing, the moment to speak can easily pass.

rows.ko: 덜 다듬어진 생각도 지금의 마음 그대로 꺼내는 힘을 키울 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 하고 싶은 말이 생기면 하루를 넘기지 말고 짧게라도 먼저 전해 보세요.
rows.en: You're ready to share your thoughts as they are, rough edges and all. In the year ahead, when there's something you want to say, say it, even briefly, before the day is out.
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your ability to share even unpolished thoughts, just as you feel them now. In the year ahead, when you have something to say, try saying it, even briefly, before the day is out.

rows.ko: 개구리
rows.en: Frog
rows.note: 캐릭터명

rows.ko: 더 좋은 때를 기다리며 말을 미뤄 두는 습관은 내려놓아 볼 만해요. 때와 자리를 고르는 신중함은 한때 대화를 순조롭게 이끌어 준 방법이지만, 꼭 맞는 때는 생각보다 잘 오지 않기 때문입니다.
rows.en: Let go of waiting for a better moment before you speak. Choosing the right time and place once kept conversations running smoothly, but the perfect moment arrives far less often than you'd think.
rows.en_before_tone: The habit of putting off what you want to say while waiting for a better moment is worth setting down. Carefully choosing the time and place once kept conversations running smoothly, but the perfect moment doesn't come along as often as you'd think.

rows.ko: 조금 어색한 때라도 필요한 말을 꺼내는 힘을 키울 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 미뤄 둔 이야기 하나를 골라 가벼운 자리에서 먼저 운을 떼 보세요.
rows.en: This is your year to say what needs saying, even when the timing feels a bit awkward. In the year ahead, pick one conversation you've been putting off and ease into it somewhere relaxed.
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your ability to say what needs saying, even when the moment feels a little awkward. In the year ahead, try picking one conversation you've been putting off and gently bringing it up in a relaxed setting.

rows.ko: 문어
rows.en: Octopus
rows.note: 캐릭터명

rows.ko: 어긋난 사이를 그날 안에 풀어야 한다는 조급함은 조금 내려놓아도 괜찮아요. 먼저 손을 내미는 힘은 한때 관계를 빨리 이어 준 방법이지만, 상대가 준비되기 전에 다가가면 오히려 마음이 닫히기 쉽기 때문입니다.
rows.en: Release the pressure to patch things up the very same day. Reaching out first once mended relationships fast, but reaching out before the other person is ready makes them close off instead.
rows.en_before_tone: It's okay to loosen the urgency to fix things the same day when something goes wrong between you. Reaching out first once reconnected relationships quickly, but reaching out before the other person is ready can actually make them close off.

rows.ko: 화해를 청한 뒤 상대의 속도를 믿고 기다리는 힘을 키울 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 다툼 뒤에 내 마음은 짧게 전하고, 답은 편할 때 해도 된다는 말을 함께 건네 보세요.
rows.en: Now you learn to offer to make up, then trust the other person's pace and wait. In the year ahead, after an argument, share how you feel in a few words and tell them they can reply whenever they're ready.
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your ability to trust the other person's pace and wait after offering to make up. In the year ahead, after an argument, try sharing your feelings briefly and adding that they can reply whenever they're ready.

rows.ko: 해파리
rows.en: Jellyfish
rows.note: 캐릭터명

rows.ko: 다툼을 빨리 덮으려 서운함을 흘려보내는 습관은 내려놓아 볼 만해요. 흐름에 맞춰 분위기를 부드럽게 만드는 힘은 한때 관계를 지켜 준 방법이지만, 말하지 않은 서운함은 다음 다툼 때 한꺼번에 올라오기 쉽기 때문입니다.
rows.en: Set aside the habit of letting hurt feelings drift by just to smooth over an argument. Going with the flow to soften the mood once protected your relationships, but hurt left unsaid comes flooding out in the next argument.
rows.en_before_tone: The habit of letting hurt drift by to quickly smooth over an argument is worth setting down. Going with the flow to soften the mood once protected your relationships, but hurt left unsaid tends to come up all at once in the next argument.

rows.ko: 관계를 지키는 일과 내 마음을 지키는 일이 함께 갈 수 있다고 믿는 힘을 키울 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 서운한 일이 생기면 한 줄 메모로 적어 두고, 쌓이기 전에 하나씩 나눠 보세요.
rows.en: Trust that caring for a relationship and caring for yourself go hand in hand. In the year ahead, when something stings, jot it down in a one-line note, and bring those notes up one at a time before they pile up.
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your trust that protecting a relationship and protecting your own heart can go together. In the year ahead, when something hurts, try jotting it down in a one-line note, and sharing those notes one at a time before they pile up.

rows.ko: 가오리
rows.en: Stingray
rows.note: 캐릭터명

rows.ko: 마음이 가라앉을 때까지 말없이 오래 혼자 떨어져 있는 습관은 조금 풀어 놓아도 돼요. 혼자 숨을 고르는 시간은 한때 후회할 말을 막아 준 방법이지만, 기약 없는 침묵은 상대에게 더 먼 거리로 느껴지기 쉽기 때문입니다.
rows.en: Ease up on going silent and keeping your distance for ages until you've cooled off. Taking time alone to calm down once kept you from saying things you'd regret, but open-ended silence feels like a far wider gap to the other person.
rows.en_before_tone: You can loosen the habit of staying apart, silent and alone, for a long time until you've calmed down. Time alone to catch your breath once kept you from saying things you'd regret, but silence with no end in sight can feel like an even greater distance to the other person.

rows.ko: 쉬는 시간을 가지면서도 돌아올 길을 열어 두는 힘을 키울 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 쉬고 돌아왔을 때 먼저 건넬 첫마디를 미리 한 문장 정해 두세요.
rows.en: Take your break, and leave the door open to come back. In the year ahead, decide in advance on the one sentence you'll say first when you return after some space.
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your ability to keep a way back open even while taking a break. In the year ahead, try deciding ahead of time on one sentence you'll say first when you come back from a break.

rows.ko: 불가사리
rows.en: Starfish
rows.note: 캐릭터명

rows.ko: 서운함을 듣기 전에 해결책부터 정리해 내미는 습관은 내려놓아도 괜찮아요. 차근차근 길을 찾는 힘은 한때 어긋난 사이를 이어 준 방법이지만, 마음이 먼저 닿지 않으면 좋은 해결책도 멀게 느껴지기 때문입니다.
rows.en: Hold back from rushing in with solutions before you've heard how the other person feels. Working step by step toward a fix once brought people back together, but if their feelings aren't heard first, even a great solution feels out of reach.
rows.en_before_tone: It's okay to set down the habit of laying out solutions before hearing the other person's hurt. Finding a way step by step once reconnected relationships that went off track, but if hearts don't connect first, even a good solution can feel far away.

rows.ko: 해결보다 먼저 상대의 마음을 알아주는 말을 건네는 힘을 키울 때입니다. 다가오는 해에는 내 생각을 말하기 전에, 상대가 한 말을 한 번 그대로 되짚어 주는 연습을 해 보세요.
rows.en: Your growth now is acknowledging how someone feels before you try to fix anything. In the year ahead, before you share your own take, practice repeating back what the other person said, in their own words.
rows.en_before_tone: Now is the time to grow your ability to offer words that acknowledge how the other person feels, before solving anything. In the year ahead, before sharing your own thoughts, try repeating back what the other person said, just as they said it.

rows.en_before_tone: This is a year when your wish for change and the movement of the sky point the same way. Change has always been familiar ground for you, so you might start by taking up the new offers that fit the direction you're hoping for.

rows.en: Little shakes things up from the outside this year, so rather than rushing change, lay its groundwork with patience. What you prepare now becomes your launchpad for the change you want.
rows.en_before_tone: With few big shifts around you this year, it's a good time to calmly build a foundation rather than rushing change. The groundwork you lay now can become a stepping stone toward the change you want.

rows.ko: 큰 변화가 적어 내가 속도를 정하기 좋은 해로, 좋고 나쁨이 아니라 움직임의 크기를 뜻합니다.

rows.en: Your life stays on an even keel this year. Steadiness is your strength, so build toward what you want, slow and steady, one day at a time.
rows.en_before_tone: This is a calm year without big shake-ups. Since steadiness is your strength, it's a good time to build toward what you're hoping for, calmly, day by day.

rows.ko: 하늘의 큰 움직임이 적어, 변화의 속도를 내가 정하기 좋은 해입니다. 서둘러 하나를 고르기보다 여러 가능성을 천천히 살펴보며, 가장 마음이 가는 방향을 찾아보세요.
rows.en: With few big planetary shifts, you set the pace of change yourself this year. Skip the rush to pick just one thing. Explore the options unhurriedly and follow the direction that pulls at you most.
rows.en_before_tone: With few big movements in the sky, this is a good year to set the pace of change yourself. Rather than rushing to pick one thing, you might take your time exploring different possibilities and find the direction your heart is most drawn to.
